meaning.levelBasis: outcome: the source assigns this outcome to this level (its code, unit, course configuration, or a single-level course). course: the source assigns no level, so the outcome is listed at every level its course offers.
meaning.units: Only units at this level, or level-less units holding an outcome at this level; outcomeIds keeps only this level's outcomes.
meaning.configurations: Only the course configurations for this level.
meaning.document: Only the document units at this level (all of them for a single-level course).

statusMeaning.imported: Copied automatically from the outcome's official page. Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.cross-checked: Copied automatically from the outcome's official page, and the Ministry's CSV file has the same words in the same order (ignoring punctuation and spacing; the CSV shortens some long statements, and then its words must match the start). Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.document-extracted: A course's `document`: copied from the text layer of the official curriculum document (PDF) by scripts/curriculum/documents/. Not yet checked by a person.
statusMeaning.document-ocr-unverified: A course's `document`: read by OCR from a scanned official curriculum document (PDF) and not proofread. Check every item against the printed page before use.

flagsMeaning.listedInMenu: The site's Browse by Subject or Browse by Grade menus link to the course (otherwise it is reachable only through the search list).
flagsMeaning.legacy: An older curriculum that a renewed one replaces; see legacyEvidence.
flagsMeaning.notACurriculum: A site entry with no curriculum behind it; see notACurriculumEvidence.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the need for accounting in business.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Accounting (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and use the language of accounting (e.g., assets, liabilities, debits, credits).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify accounting related career opportunities (e.g., bookkeeping, general office work, clerk, payroll, receivables, payables).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Define financial accounting, cost accounting and management accounting.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize forms of business ownership including sole proprietorship, corporation, franchise, partnership, and a cooperative model.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how different forms of business ownership have led to the need for different accounting practices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: List and classify types of business enterprises (e.g., resources, manufacturing, merchandising and service) within local community, Saskatchewan, Canada and globally.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how different types of business enterprises (e.g., resources, manufacturing, merchandising and service) require different accounting practices.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the role/purpose of accounting from the perspective of a manufacturer, producer, wholesaler, retailer, consumer and citizen in the business world.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how accountants’ training and practices will vary according to the type of employer (e.g., manufacturer, producer, retailer) and job description.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the inquiry question: Why is accounting important?

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Label the steps of the accounting cycle (i.e., analyze originating transaction data, journalize, post, prepare worksheets, prepare financial statements, journalize and post adjusting and closing entries, prepare post-closing trial balance).

outcomes.statement: Explain the role of accounting standards.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Identifying Accounting Standards (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize that accounting handbooks exist to ensure accounting practices reflect current standards.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List examples of accounting principles (e.g., Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles [GAAPs]; business identity, going concern, accounting period cycle, objective evidence, unit of measurement, realization of revenue, matching expenses with revenue, historical cost, adequate disclosure, consistent reporting).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Relate accounting standards to examples found in the community (e.g., local business, First Nations governance authorities, not-for-profit organizations, public sector entities).

outcomes.statement: Analyze the relationship between assets, liabilities and owners’ equity within the accounting equation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Accounting Equation (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1, 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define assets, liabilities and owners’ equity (capital).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify and sort examples of assets, liabilities and owners’ equity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the accounting equation relationship (i.e., a = l + oe).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Manipulate and solve problems using the accounting equation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine how business transactions affect the accounting equation and apply to calculations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the preservation of equality (e.g., increasing assets impacts liabilities and owners’ equity) within the accounting equation.

outcomes.statement: Utilize transactions and apply T-accounts in order to understand the concept of an account.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: T-accounts (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Relate the left and right of the T-account location to the accounting equation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Label debit (left) and credit (right) as left and right of the T-account location.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the location (l/r) of the elements (i.e., assets, liabilities, owners’ equity) of the accounting equation and how those elements correlate to the normal balance of an account.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Implement the use of normal balance in each sub-element of owners’ equity (i.e., capital [CR], drawings [DR], revenue [CR] and expenses [DR]).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Interpret how the normal balance side of a T-account relates to the increase and decrease of an account balance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize and apply the concept of double entry accounting by assigning the amounts of a transaction into one debit and one credit part.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze transactions into debits and credits using a pair of T-accounts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze a full set of business transactions and record in a ledger of T-accounts.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Calculate the final balance of a T-account.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Prove equality between normal debit balances and normal credit balances by totaling accounts to confirm the accounting equation.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss how capital, drawings, revenue and expenses relate to owners’ equity.

outcomes.statement: Explore how journals simplify and organize transactions in accounting.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Journals (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the information contained in source documents.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Justify the importance of a journal as a permanent legal entity or legal document as it connects to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAPs).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify columns (i.e., general debit, general credit, special amount columns) of a combination journal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze and record business transactions into a journal or journals referencing a chart of accounts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Prove the total of debit columns equals the total of credit columns.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prove cash by determining that the amount of cash in the journal agrees with the accounting records (e.g., cheque stub).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze, explain and correct discrepancies when preparing a series of accounting proofs such as slide, divide by 9, and double/half.

outcomes.statement: Summarize transactions of an account by updating ledgers to obtain current balance.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Ledgers (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a chart of accounts and sort assets (100), liabilities (200), capital (300), revenue (400) and expenses (500) into numerical order for a service business organized as a proprietorship.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the columns (e.g., date, name, account, number, account number, entry, balance) of a ledger form and open a ledger for each account.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the need for a ledger (i.e., balance of accounts) when a journal is already done.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Post amounts from the general debit and credit columns into individual accounts in the general ledger.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Post totals from the special amount columns to individual accounts.

outcomes.statement: Create a worksheet to summarize data in order to generate financial statements.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Worksheets (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 6

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prove the ledger by preparing a trial balance in the worksheet which includes listing all account titles and balances from the general ledgers into correct debit and credit columns.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Calculate and record adjustments in the worksheet in accordance with the Generally Accepted Accounting Principle (GAAP) matching principle.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Extend the revenue and expense accounts into the income statement from the trial balance and adjustments column.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Extend the assets, liabilities, capital, and drawing accounts to the balance sheet column from the trial balance and adjustment column.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Total the columns of the income statement and calculate net income/net loss with proving totals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the relationship between sales and expenses (i.e., net income or net loss) on the worksheet.

outcomes.statement: Prepare and interpret financial statements (income statement and balance sheet) for an accounting period.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Financial Statements (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss how recording and reporting financial information affects business owners’ ability to make accurate business decisions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Consider the inquiry questions: How are financial statements used to aid decision makers? What information must be present on a financial statement (e.g., adequate disclosure)?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose of income statements and balance sheets.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compile the income statement listing the heading, business name, date, account titles and appropriate debit and credit amounts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Calculate the net income or loss by comparing the revenue and expenses to ensure the net income/loss on the income statement is consistent with the worksheet.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize that a balance sheet reports the financial condition of a business on a specific date by detailing the assets, liabilities and capital.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compile a balance sheet listing business name, date, account titles and appropriate amounts for the assets and liabilities using the amounts from the worksheet’s balance sheet columns.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Calculate the capital for a balance sheet ensuring that total assets equal total liabilities and capital.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Critique a presentation of financial statements from the perspective of a member of the board of directors or from the perspective of a potential investor.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess the viability of a business based on a simulated balance sheet.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Analyze examples of publicly available financial statements.

outcomes.statement: Generate adjusting and closing entries in relation to the appropriate accounting period.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Adjusting and Closing Entries (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how the matching principle justifies the need for adjusting and closing entries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Record adjusting entries in the general or combination journal for all prepaid expenses (e.g., supplies, insurance, advertising).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Transfer the adjusting entries from the general or combination journal to the ledger by posting them to appropriate ledger account.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Distinguish between permanent and temporary accounts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the new account income summary as a temporary account.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Define and discuss the purpose of closing entries (e.g., update accounts, transferring net income/loss to owners’ equity account).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Calculate and prepare closing entries by journalizing each entry and posting them to the ledger to bring temporary accounts to zero.

outcomes.statement: Explore the final step of the accounting cycle.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Post-Closing Trial Balance (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define post-closing trial balance and its purpose.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prove the equality between debits and credits of the permanent accounts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Rationalize why no temporary accounts will be in the post-closing trial balance.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the end-of-the month permanent account balances are new balances for the next month.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the inquiry question: Why is it important to complete the post-closing trial balance at the end of a fiscal period?

outcomes.statement: Examine accounting practices through application of the accounting cycle for service business scenarios.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Accounting Cycle Project (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply the accounting cycle (i.e., analyze originating transaction data, journalize, post, prepare worksheets, prepare financial statements, journalize and post adjusting and closing entries, prepare post-closing trial balance) to a service business scenario.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Apply error finding techniques within aspects of the accounting cycle and identify appropriate corrections.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss and justify decisions made to solve problems that arise during the accounting cycle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze decisions for given scenarios utilizing the accounting cycle.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the financial situation of a service business based on the financial statements.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compose questions to help accountants interpret and analyze financial statements.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare post-closing trial balances for two different accounting cycles and examine changes that occurred during the accounting period.

outcomes.statement: Justify the importance of wellness practices for employers and employees.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Employee Wellness (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research practices that impact employee productivity, profit and retention.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify factors (e.g., snacks, atmosphere, movement opportunities) that influence employee wellness.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the impact that sitting at a desk or computer has on physical and mental wellness.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform stretches designed for employees that are working at a desk or computer for extended periods.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design a company policy regarding employee wellness.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify ergonomic risk factors and plan an ergonomic work station.

outcomes.statement: Investigate career opportunities in the accounting industry in Saskatchewan and Canada.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13A: Career Opportunities in Accounting (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify occupations in the accounting industry (e.g., public accounting, industry, government).

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s suitability or non-suitability for a specific occupation in the accounting industry.

outcomes.statement: Investigate payroll and how net pay is calculated.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25A: Basic Payroll (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize the components including gross pay, deductions and net pay of a pay cheque.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the gross pay, deductions and net pay on a given document.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Calculate the gross pay, total deductions and net pay.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the gross pay to the net pay.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) website for current Canadian tax information.

outcomes.statement: Investigate technology as a tool to aid in the accounting process.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29A: Technology Applications for a Service Business (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the various types and purposes of accounting software.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the use of computers and accounting software in service business accounting.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify key issues to consider when dealing with software copyright and site licensing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the importance of restricting access to data by using a password/security system.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose solutions to accounting problems where accounting software has been used.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Review the accounting cycle of a service business relating manual activities to those that may be performed using accounting software.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate how service businesses in the community use accounting software.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Carry out an accounting cycle for a service business using accounting software.

outcomes.statement: Investigate different types of businesses and options for ownership.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30: Business Types and Ownership Options (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify various forms of business ownership including sole proprietorship, partnership and corporations including cooperatives.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Summarize components of sole proprietorship, partnership, or incorporation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: List different types of businesses such as merchandising, manufacturing, service and e-commerce.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Distinguish which businesses found in the local community are sole proprietorship, partnerships and corporations.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate businesses found in the province of Saskatchewan, in Canada and globally.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the inquiry question: How is a corporation like a democratic government structure (e.g., provincial government, city/town council, First Nations Band Council)?

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the contributions that different organizations or businesses (e.g., cooperatives, Crown Corporations, First Nations band councils and Métis communities) have made to Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research how the lifestyles and worldviews of First Nations peoples impact decisions related to business organization (e.g., benefit of the community compared to the benefit of the individual).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research ownership structures that are permitted on First Nations land as it relates to the implications of the Indian Act (e.g., A First Nation band is not a corporation).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Present the characteristics and process of forming partnerships and/or corporations.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Generate a simple partnership agreement (e.g., a partnership must always equal 100 percent but does not need to be 50/50) based on an example in an area of interest.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Create a simple articles of incorporation for a corporation based on an area of interest.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Construct and explain a business ownership solution (sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation) based on given scenarios.

courses.name: Agriculture Production A10, B10, A20, B20, A30, B30

outcomes.statement: Investigate the impact and significance of agriculture in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Agriculture (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine agriculture's connections to Saskatchewan's economy.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Apply terms commonly associated with the agriculture industry in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe related services that support agriculture production (e.g., research, storage and transportation).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore Saskatchewan's agricultural value regarding growing, processing and exporting food for provincial, national and global markets.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how agriculture, carbon sequestration, and sustainable agriculture practices can be part of nature-based climate solutions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify current events, trends and issues (e.g., population growth and climate change) affecting the agriculture industry in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of major events offered in Saskatchewan that promote agriculture.

outcomes.statement: Explore the role of injury prevention and safety in agriculture production.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Introduction to Farm Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the types and frequency of common farm preventable injuries by analyzing industry statistics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the hierarchy of controls to control hazards and mitigate risks in various agriculture workspaces and environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze and describe the effect of lost production time due to equipment damage or personal injury during critical times of the year (e.g., seeding, harvest, calving).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the effect that costs of equipment damage have on production profit margins (e.g., down time, repair costs, insurance costs).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore ways to mitigate risk of damage to equipment (e.g., maintenance schedule, pre-use inspections, scheduled inspections, understanding manufacturer's recommendations and reporting damage).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the positive and negative effects to using each category (e.g., respiratory, hearing, vision, skin and body) of industry standard personal protective equipment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify sections of the Saskatchewan Employment Act that apply to owners, employers, contractors, supervisors, suppliers, self-employed persons and workers as it relates to agriculture production operations.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify when an Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) program is required by law for an agriculture production operation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the worker's three rights: the right to know, the right to participate and the right to refuse unsafe work.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research the benefits of completing certifications and programs offered by Work Safe Sask (Mental Health and Wellness, Occupational Health and Safety and Young Career Worker Readiness), Sask Safety Council (Online Agriculture Training System - OATS and Career Safety Education), Motor Safety Association (Introduction to Workplace Safety), Agricultural Health and Safety Network (Respiratory Health in Ag), Sask Prevention (Farm Safety) and the Ministry of Labour Relations and Workplace Safety (Farm Safety).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe basic response plans for common types of emergencies in agriculture operations (e.g., fire, medical aid, entrapment, violent threat, severe storms).

outcomes.statement: Apply proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Farm Chemical Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the importance of, and methods used for, maintenance of a clean and safe workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify important information categories from product labels, Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and manufacturer's chemical information packages such as compatibility, storage requirements, application method, preharvest intervals and withdrawal periods.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the four parts of Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) (i.e., labels with warning symbols, hazard identification and product classification, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), worker education and worksite specific training).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the different hazards, identifiers and uses of consumer products, control products, and pesticides.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and intended use of the mandatory information on a pesticide label as regulated by Health Canada.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the types of hazardous materials that an agricultural operation might create.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the potential heath risks of exposure to chemicals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate record keeping strategies for maintaining SDS information.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore training and certification opportunities (e.g., WHMIS and pesticide applicator licence) on the safe use of agricultural chemicals.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the uses of agricultural chemicals that would require a Saskatchewan Pesticide Applicator Licence.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe handling of chemical products using approved safety gear.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise the safe storage of chemical products.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop procedures for handling mishaps such as chemical spills.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss first-aid procedures for exposure to agricultural chemicals (e.g., fertilizer, pesticide, fuel and anhydrous ammonia).

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Investigate regulations and responsibilities to safely dispose of leftover chemical and chemical containers.

outcomes.statement: Apply proper handling of hazardous materials to prevent injury in the workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3B: Farm Chemical Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the importance of, and methods used for, maintenance of a clean and safe workplace.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify important information categories from product labels, Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and manufacturer's chemical information packages such as compatibility, storage requirements, application method, preharvest intervals and withdrawal periods.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the four parts of Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) (i.e., labels with warning symbols, hazard identification and product classification, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), worker education and worksite specific training).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the different hazards, identifiers and uses of consumer products, control products, and pesticides.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and intended use of the mandatory information on a pesticide label as regulated by Health Canada.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the types of hazardous materials that an agricultural operation might create.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the potential heath risks of exposure to chemicals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate record keeping strategies for maintaining SDS information.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore training and certification opportunities (e.g., WHMIS and pesticide applicator licence) on the safe use of agricultural chemicals.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the uses of agricultural chemicals that would require a Saskatchewan Pesticide Applicator Licence.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe handling of chemical products using approved safety gear.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise the safe storage of chemical products.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop procedures for handling mishaps such as chemical spills.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss first-aid procedures for exposure to agricultural chemicals (e.g., fertilizer, pesticide, fuel and anhydrous ammonia).

outcomes.statement: Investigate holistic approaches to positive psychological health and safety.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Psychological Health and Safety - Personal (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine how psychological health forms part of a person's physical, mental, emotional and spiritual well-being.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the factors (e.g., loss of a loved one, divorce, poor farm year caused by drought and imbalances in chemical, neurological, hormonal and biological systems) that may contribute to mental illness.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of social media, culture, lack of community resources and an unsupportive social network on mental health.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Examine the effects that experiences (e.g., residential schools and inter-generational trauma and farm accident) can have on individuals and communities.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify risky behaviours (e.g., alcohol, drugs, gang affiliation and toxic relationships) that can impact positive psychological health.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze how Western, Indigenous, traditional, complementary and alternative approaches to health care can contribute to a holistic perspective of psychological health.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss examples of misconceptions and stigmas associated with mental illness within society.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify feelings (e.g., embarrassment, shame and resentment) and behaviours (e.g., abandonment, exclusion and rejection) resulting from societal stigma.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss valuable skills (e.g., positive self-perception, effective communication, stress management and a positive social network) for maintaining positive psychological health.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the history of Indigenous agriculture.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: History of Indigenous Agriculture (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the importance of the relationship First Nations and Métis peoples have with the land.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss Indigenous perspectives on agriculture and their connections to the land with an Elder or Knowledge Keeper.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of settlers on Indigenous agricultural practices.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the agriculture clauses found in the numbered treaties from 1871-1921.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the difficulties Indigenous farmers experienced through the creation of the Indian Act of 1876. (e.g., the pass and permit system from the late 1800s up to and including 1951).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the significance of traditional farming methods (e.g., Three Sisters crop model and planting a fish with corn seed) developed by First Nations and Métis communities.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the importance of the role of bison for First Nations and Métis peoples.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the impact the mass elimination of bison had on Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the inclusion of agriculture (e.g., livestock and farming implements) in the numbered treaties.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss the importance to the First Nations peoples of agriculture being included in the numbered treaties.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explain the role of livestock (e.g., oxen, horses and cattle) in early Indigenous farming practices.

outcomes.statement: Explore how livestock and crop production information is gathered and interpreted.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Information Gathering (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the need for reliable information in all production sectors.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the reliability of a source of gathered information.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Locate, organize and clarify information in a variety of formats (e.g., spreadsheets, concept webs and graphs).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Interpret animal health labels (e.g., medications) and crop input product information (e.g., product labels on pharmaceuticals, fertilizers and pesticides).

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Identify available government and private sector services in the production of livestock and crops.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore sources of information on livestock and crop production (e.g., Saskatchewan Ministry of Agriculture and The Western Producer).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Read technical information from an information management system (IMS).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Analyze livestock and crop production information from various sources (e.g., blogs/vlogs, Saskatchewan Soil Information System [SKSIS] and Community Collaborative Rain, Hail and Snow Network [CoCoRHS]).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore programs and services that do not align with First Nations policy and cannot be used by First Nations peoples.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of water stewardship in sustainable agriculture production.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Water Stewardship (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a watershed and its relationship to agriculture production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a map showing the geographic boundaries for Saskatchewan's major watersheds.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the characteristics (e.g., size, slope, shape, drainage, land use and cover, geology and soils) of the local watershed.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Research historical and contemporary issues associated with livestock production and water stewardship.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the role of Saskatchewan's Water Security Agency in maintaining water safety and security in the province.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore Indigenous perspectives on water security.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the creation, types and characteristics of soil.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10A: Soil (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain how soils are formed from their parent material.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the different types of soil.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Construct a map showing the soil zones in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the characteristics of soil types including structure and horizons, tilth, density and porosity, particle size, color, compaction and texture.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the main components of soil (e.g., organic and inorganic material, water and air).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the properties of water.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe how water moves in soil.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify regions of Saskatchewan that still contain virgin soil.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the relationship between climate and agriculture.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Climate (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of how glaciation and climate have shaped Saskatchewan's agricultural land to what it is today.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze how climate and weather influence Saskatchewan agriculture.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the cost of climate change on the agriculture industry (e.g., fertilizer sales, crop yield and feed shortage).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore how agricultural practices can adapt to climate change and variability.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how the increase in human population and resources directly impact agriculture.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe how agricultural crops and livestock can be a carbon source or a carbon sink and how that can affect climate change.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how sustainable agriculture practices can form part of nature-based climate solutions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of the earth maintaining a carbon balance.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of a livestock production facility.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12A: Livestock Facility Design (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Describe the purposes and benefits of different types of livestock housing (e.g., stall barns and loose housing).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare different types of rails and wire fencing (e.g., barbed, woven, cable, mesh and electric) including factors such as cost, potential injury to animals and workers and suitability for different livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of temporary and permanent fencing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the cost, availability, effectiveness, animal safety and worker safety of equipment options (e.g., cages, chutes, corrals, gates and pens) for sorting, handling and loading livestock.

outcomes.statement: Design a livestock farmyard.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12B: Livestock Farmyard Design (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 12A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research advantages and disadvantages of construction material (e.g., steel or wood frame and exterior material) and shape of farm buildings.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of overhead and underground power lines and identify ways to mitigate the risks.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate water sources (e.g., well, dug-out and sand point), testing for livestock and human consumption and their proximity to wastewater systems (e.g., sewage).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the use of alternative sources of energy (e.g., backup generator, windmill, solar panels and geothermal).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe an effective system (e.g., burning barrel and recycling program) for solid waste disposal.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify security options (e.g., security cameras, fencing and dogs) for livestock farms.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the importance of fire guards within a farmyard.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify characteristics and options for fuel and chemical storage.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain how to deter and remove pests and rodents.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify characteristics and options for emergency shelters from severe storms (e.g., tornado and plow winds).

indicators.label: k

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Analyze the cost, availability, effectiveness, maintenance requirements and worker safety of storage options (e.g., hopper bottom, flat bottom, round and square bins, grain bags, elevators, piles and Quonsets) for grain and fertilizer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the manufacturer's recommendations for anchoring grain and fertilizer bins.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the unique characteristics of specialty crop storage and transportation (e.g., refrigeration for fruits and vegetables and bags for wild rice).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of grain and fertilizer storage (e.g., protection from moisture, vegetation control, bin identification and access).

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the design and operation of different types of irrigation equipment (e.g., pumps, piping, pivot, wheel-move and hand-move).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply basic repair and maintenance skills to buildings, vegetation and roads.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify ways to mitigate the safety and health risks of entering a storage building.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss ways to mitigate the safety risks of climbing on top of storage structures (e.g., grain bins).

b

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: j

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate effective communication skills.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Effective Communication in Agriculture (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of effective communication skills (e.g., speaking, writing, listening and reading) for those employed in agriculture.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the characteristics of effective verbal and written communication (e.g., specific language choice, simple instructions and concise answers).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe types of communication (e.g., reading and interpreting animal health products and manuals, discussing farm equipment needs with suppliers, rates of weight gain and seed and crop protection guides) required in agriculture production.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why communication is a critical component of safety procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the role that negotiation plays in effective business communication.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research negotiation strategies to acquire better business deals within the agriculture industry.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify communication tools (e.g., video conferencing, broadcast media and social media), the skills required to effectively use them and when they might be used in agriculture production.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of communication between producers, industry (e.g., equipment manufacturers), consumers and the public about production practices.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the protocols to be followed to share information with First Nations individuals and communities.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify resources (e.g., Agriculture in the Classroom and Farm & Food Care Saskatchewan) specific to agriculture topics.

outcomes.statement: Examine animal breed characteristics and development.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21A: Animal Breeds (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the proper terms for the gender of livestock animals (e.g., steer, heifer, colt, filly, hen and ewe).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the main distinguishing physical characteristics (e.g., age, frame, size and weight) of an ideal specimen of a chosen livestock breed.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify qualities (e.g., age, health and undesirable physical characteristics) to be considered when culling livestock from a specific type of livestock operation (e.g., beef breeding and dairy farms).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Summarize the relationship between purebred breeders and commercial operations.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of expected progeny differences (EPD) when breeding cattle.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the introduction of new livestock to the prairies by early settlers.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the development of desired characteristics of livestock through breeding practices of the First Nations and Métis peoples and early settlers.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the benefits of crossbreeding.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: List the strengths and weaknesses of several breeds of a chosen livestock species.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Classify breeds of a chosen livestock species according to their purpose.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore the codes and practices for a chosen livestock species.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Investigate organizations that maintain a breed registry in Canada.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Discuss the development of exotic livestock (e.g., ostrich and llama) farming in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Explore how horses were introduced to First Nations peoples and why they are important to their culture.

outcomes.statement: Examine animal breed behaviours.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21B: Animal Breed Behaviours (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 21A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore behaviours of livestock including herd instinct, characteristics of the social hierarchy in a herd and flight distance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe basic livestock needs (e.g., comfort, reproduction, exercise, food, communication, survival and protection).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how livestock respond to various stimuli (e.g., response [positive], reaction [negative], acceptance and tolerance) in their environment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how a handler should react to livestock responding to specific stimuli (e.g., moving to different surroundings, loud noises, changes in weather and dogs).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and explain possible causes of vices (e.g., teeth grinding, rearing, biting and difficulty in catching).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate handler techniques designed to minimize risks to animal and worker health and prevent injuries.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to handle different animal breeds according to their behavioural characteristics.

outcomes.statement: Explore safe methods of working around, and handling, livestock under stress.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22A: Basic Handling - Stress (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 21A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the effects of stress in livestock on their health and production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize the characteristics of an animal under stress (e.g., agitated or aggressive behaviour and flight risk).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how a handler's body language (e.g., aggressive behaviour) affects livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the use of safe handler behaviours (e.g., slow movements, calm tone of voice, avoid cornering livestock and maintaining an escape route) when approaching and working with livestock under stress.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate and explain how to approach an animal safely using ground manners (e.g., scope of vision).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a plan for handling livestock experiencing stressful situations (e.g., injured animal and death of the queen bee) and emergency situations (e.g., barn fire and livestock struck by vehicle).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the accepted methods for properly euthanizing livestock in the least painful and most humane way.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the benefits of proper bedding and housing design (e.g., stall size, hive structure, base, floor grooving, scratchers and location of waterers) on animal comfort.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the factors affecting livestock nutrition.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23A: Livestock Nutrition (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify common food sources (e.g., hay, grain, forages and additives) for a specific livestock species and their role in the livestock's diet.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare feed storage options.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess hay quality based on a list of criteria (e.g., quantity of stems or seed, color and odour).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the importance and methods of feed testing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze different livestock watering methods.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the importance of proper feeding routines (e.g., time of day, frequency and locations).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe physiological responses to changes in feed (e.g., colic and founder).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss problems associated with inadequate nutrition and insufficient water intake.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate the proper use of livestock handling equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24A: Livestock Handling Equipment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the safe operation of large handling equipment (e.g., squeezes, head gates and chutes) to prevent animal and worker injury when moving livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the types and operation of different gates to manage the movement of livestock.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Practise proper use of hand-held tools (e.g., prods, whips and control poles) for managing livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the use of animal identification equipment (e.g., brander, tagger and microchips).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use small equipment (e.g., shears, hoof trimmer and grooming gear) to care for livestock.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare equipment used for handling large (e.g., cattle, horses and bison) and small (e.g., pork, chickens and sheep) livestock.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform cleaning and sanitizing procedures of livestock handling equipment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the use of scales to weigh different types of livestock.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the assessment of livestock health.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25A: Livestock Health Care - Assessment (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore welfare assessment tools as recommended by the Canadian Council on Animal Care (CCAC).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform an evaluation of an animal's vital signs including temperature, pulse and respiratory rate and recognize when additional care may be required.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of common livestock injuries, disorders and diseases.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess livestock injuries, disorders and diseases to determine if veterinary care is required.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the recognition and significance of conformation faults and blemishes in livestock.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how body condition scoring is used to assess the health of different types of animals.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe livestock dental and hoof issues that require treatment.

outcomes.statement: Explore production of livestock products in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify animal products (e.g., eggs, milk, honey, wool and meat) produced in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the quality grades (e.g., choice, standard and utility) used for meat products.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the variation in terminology for specific cuts of meat in different livestock in the American system and other cultures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the characteristics of the meat produced by different types of livestock (e.g., bison, cattle and chickens).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain why different breeds of a species of livestock are used for different purposes (e.g., wool versus meat sheep, milk versus beef cattle and egg laying versus meat chickens).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe equipment (e.g., egg packer, milking machine and honey extractor) used for a specific livestock product.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate the safe operation of a piece of equipment used for a specific livestock product following the manufacturer's direction.

outcomes.statement: Explore the attributes of ideal pastures.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the optimum plant composition of a pasture for a specific species of livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Describe optimal pasture conditions, including:
- clean and sufficient water supply;
- abundant and healthy vegetation cover; and,
- natural shelter and shade.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify invasive plants in pastures and why they are a problem.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss clean water management practices such as fencing dugouts, protecting riparian areas and preventing algae growth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the components of a pasture (e.g., mineral tubs and water containers) that require regular inspection and maintenance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare the use of tame and native pasture.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the positive and negative impacts of livestock on the land and carbon cycle.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss why native prairie is considered an endangered ecosystem.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore why some land is used for pasture instead of crop farming.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of data, and the tools used to support livestock record keeping.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of collecting data and maintaining livestock records.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the necessity of maintaining routines (e.g., pen checks every day, milking at the same time and monitoring breeding season) and collecting data where appropriate.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the use of computer software and spreadsheets designed for keeping livestock records.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to collect and organize information into a list, table, graph or chart.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate how record keeping is essential to following commodity specific programs like beef's VBP+ or dairy's ProAction.

indicators.label: b

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the use of computer software and spreadsheets designed for keeping crop records.

indicators.label: d

indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of organic livestock farming.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the steps to become a certified organic livestock producer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the methods used to reduce livestock stress (e.g., reduced caging or confinement like chaining, avoiding under stimulation and overcrowding).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss how organic farming differs from conventional farming (e.g., green manure usage, manipulation of seeding dates and seeding rates, strategic tillage for weed control, types of organic fertilizers that can be used and strategic usage of crop rotation to control insects, weeds and diseases).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of organic crop farming.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare organic biodynamic farming.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how organic crop farming principles can be used in conventional operations.

indicators.text: Outline the steps to become a certified organic crop producer.

indicators.text: Explain the significance of, and the organizations (e.g., Ecocert, Pro-cert or TransCanada Organic [TCO]) involved in, organic certification.

courses.subject: Languages

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic metacognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- construct a plan for new learning tasks with the guidance of the teacher;
- reflect on the communication process by checking copied signing for accuracy; or,
- keep a learning log to gain awareness of which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- seek the assistance of a friend to interpret text;
- repeat what someone has signed to confirm mutual understanding; or,
- recognize common facial expressions as part of ASL communication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic interpretive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- replay familiar self-chosen recorded video texts to enhance understanding and enjoyment;
- use gestures, illustrations and contextual clues to aid comprehension of unfamiliar signs; or,
- endeavour to read finger-spelled words as whole units rather than letter by letter.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to begin expressing oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic cognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- identify similarities and differences between aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- imitate signed words and sentences; or,
- memorize new sign vocabulary by repeating it or signing/finger-spelling it.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- recognize and respond to turn-taking cues;
- check with peers or teacher regarding accuracy of sign choice and production; or,
- experiment with basic forms of expression in simple conversations and note their acceptance or non-acceptance by more experienced signers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic productive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- increase signing vocabulary by copying what others sign, practising signs that are visible in the immediate environment and using resources;
- supplement signed communications with a variety of non-verbal cues (e.g., mime, pointing, gesturing, drawing pictures, illustrations, dramatization); or,
- apply knowledge of iconic signs that look like their intended meaning (e.g., eat, drink, sit) to communicate meaning by experimenting with other similar iconic signs.

outcomes.statement: Construct, with support, the meaning of simple signed texts in American Sign Language.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and understand the complete manual alphabet, basic ASL hand shapes and numbers 1 – 20.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Comprehend a repertoire of high frequency words and phrases used to communicate in predictable contexts such as when with friends and family or during holidays.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the relationships between common handshapes and location of signs, common facial expressions and their role in making different meanings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify basic ASL structures such as questions and statements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: View and understand, in guided situations, a variety of visuals and other media and communication forms (e.g., charts, graphics, illustrations, videos, digital media) to aid in signing comprehension.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the cultural influences on signed language including Plains Indian Sign Language, Langue des Signes Québécoise (LSQ) and Black American Sign Language.

outcomes.statement: Produce, with support, simple signed texts that demonstrate basic understanding of American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: *For further information and suggestions for additional grammatical elements, see Appendix B.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate basic conversational conventions (e.g., greeting, nodding in acknowledgment).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Produce complete manual alphabet, basic ASL hand shapes and the numbers 1 – 20.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Combine high frequency words and phrases to communicate with basic signed sentences in predictable contexts such as greetings, sharing basic personal information or activities in the home.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Indicate intent of communication clearly using basic ASL structures such as questions and statements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Express meaning, in guided situations, using a variety of visuals and other media and communication forms.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise, with the assistance of a model of specific linguistic elements, grammatical elements* such as gender signs, yes/no questions or cardinal and ordinal numbers.

outcomes.statement: Apply knowledge of American Sign Language, in predictable situations and for basic purposes, to receive information, extend knowledge of the world, achieve objectives and for enjoyment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the main idea from simple signed texts on predictable topics such as local community or activities in the home.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Interpret and follow simple signed instructions to complete a task.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Make, and express in writing, personal observations regarding a signed text.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compile and organize details, such as the sequence of events or steps, from signed text.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and describe the main character(s), the main problem or the purpose in simple signed stories.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Represent comprehension of a signed text in a variety of ways (e.g., demonstrations, chart, graph, concept map).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze information given in a signed presentation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Retrieve details, with guidance (e.g., with note-taking or advance organizers), from a signed video or live conversation among multiple participants.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize simple techniques used to convey humour in ASL (e.g., body movement, facial expressions).

outcomes.statement: Apply knowledge of American Sign Language, in predictable situations and for basic purposes, to impart information, share emotions and personal perspectives, achieve objectives and for enjoyment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply a repertoire of high-frequency signed vocabulary and short phrases to initiate conversations and communicate in simple interactions about concrete and predictable contexts such as local events or money.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Ask simple questions regarding basic information to find out more about topics such as friends and family or the world of work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Give simple instructions regarding a procedure or a task that relates to predictable contexts such as technology and media or activities in the home.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Express personal preferences and basic emotions regarding predictable contexts such as sports or meals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create simple signed stories that consist of a sequence of events.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise gaining the attention of a group by learning and applying Deaf conventions (e.g., shoulder tapping, stomping on the ground, flickering lights).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Use ASL for entertainment and personal enjoyment (e.g., express humour, perform skits or songs, create stories).

indicators.label: f

outcomes.statement: Incorporate more than one art form in an individual or collaborative multidisciplinary arts expression.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate examples of multidisciplinary projects as potential sources of inspiration for individual or collaborative work.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore ways of combining more than one art form (e.g., combine soundscape with dance, use visual imagery in drama, create video including music, dance, costumes and visual effects).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss challenges encountered and problems solved when engaging in multidisciplinary work.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how some individual artists use multiple art forms within their own work.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create, individually or collaboratively, an arts expression using more than one art form and/or other discipline (e.g., arts, sciences, math).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Document and reflect on own progress during, and at the conclusion of, a multidisciplinary arts expression.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with ways of communicating ideas to others, creatively through the arts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine different ways of communicating messages through the arts (e.g., compare how different artists convey a similar message, examine the same issue from different artists’ perspectives) and use as inspiration for own work.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Apply techniques and skills to express ideas.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Communicate, through arts expressions, thoughts and feelings about a topic of interest.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Take risks and discuss the value of mistakes and challenges in contributing to growth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Practise ways of providing constructive feedback throughout the creative process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the communication of ideas and intent of own work.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with personal preferences, media, styles and techniques to develop artistic voice.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the meaning of artistic voice and share examples.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on own ideas and preferences in development of artistic voice.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Take inventory of own interests and strengths in the arts and reflect on how those are connected to artistic voice.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Express an idea in several different ways and reflect on personal artistic preferences (e.g., learn a dance sequence and represent it in Bollywood, robotic, country or contemporary style).

outcomes.statement: Collaborate within an arts community.

indicators.text: Practise being part of a school-based arts community (e.g., contributing ideas, encouraging others’ work, demonstrating focus and leadership).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine different roles in a school-based arts community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how to take and give constructive feedback and apply to class discussions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Discuss inquiry questions, such as:

- How does feedback help me grow?

outcomes.statement: Investigate how the arts can challenge, reinforce or draw attention to ideas, values and/or beliefs.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Provide examples of arts expressions that challenge ideas, values and/or beliefs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Provide examples of arts expressions that reinforce or highlight ideas, values and/or beliefs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine arts expressions of First Nations and Métis artists whose work challenges or draws attention to contemporary issues of concern to Indigenous communities (e.g., treaty education outcome TPP10 – investigate issues related to resource development and treaties).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the background of the artist and context in which the selected work was created.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine how ideas and/or themes evolve in the arts as the world changes (e.g., influence of newcomer artists, evolving technologies).

outcomes.statement: Identify skills, strengths and interests and set goals for continued growth in the arts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on own skills, strengths and interests in the arts (e.g., What do you have to offer? What are your skills and competencies? What are your strengths?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a personal learning plan for continued development and involvement in the arts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore opportunities to apply artistic abilities in school and communities.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze and explore ways that creative interests, skills and competencies, learned from the arts, could apply to life after high school.

outcomes.statement: Analyze how the arts can express identity and culture, past and present.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss and investigate ways the arts can express personal and cultural identity (e.g., gender and sexual diversity, newcomer worldviews, pop culture associations).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the role of traditional and contemporary arts in expressing Indigenous cultural and individual identity, past and present (e.g., treaty education outcome SI10: Analyze the spirit and intent of treaties and investigate the extent to which they have been fulfilled).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Communicate own understanding about relationships between arts, culture and identity (e.g., present to teacher or peers).

outcomes.statement: Examine various creative processes and ways of thinking.

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Research innovative responses to problems and explore how they can be overcome through different ways of thinking in various fields of work (e.g., STEAM disciplines).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a visual representation that compares and contrasts different ways of thinking or solving problems (e.g., design, science, math, music, robotics, technology).

outcomes.statement: Research artists who create work in response to the natural world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Generate questions for inquiry regarding artists who are inspired by nature. For example:
- How do artists use materials from nature?
- How do First Nations and Métis artists express cultural and historical connections to the land?
- How did nature inspire a selected artwork (e.g., comments on sustainability, seasonal imagery in Japanese art)?

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Research artists who are inspired by the natural world such as:
- eco-friendly artists, soundscapes composers, place-based performance artists; or,
- First Nations drummers, singers, dancers and regalia designers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Document the research process (e.g., digital documentation, research notes, journal entries).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Share research findings with peers and/or others (e.g., in person, virtual presentations).
