indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the importance of personal hygiene and using personal protective equipment (e.g., gloves) for food safety.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss causes of food borne illnesses.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate common symptoms (e.g., vomiting, diarrhea, cramps, bloating) of food poisoning.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the importance of proper food storage (e.g., dried, frozen, refrigerated, food-safe containers) in safe food handling.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of safe thawing practices using various methods (i.e., cool running water, microwave, refrigerator).

indicators.text: Research best practices (e.g., proper food storage, wearing and changing gloves, using separate equipment) involved in mitigating the risk of cross-contamination for individuals with severe food allergies.

indicators.text: Explore aspects of food contamination such as how it occurs and how to identify spoiled food.

indicators.text: Determine safe food temperature zones for various foods (e.g., poultry, egg dishes, pork, beef).

indicators.text: Analyze the conditions (e.g., temperature, time, acidity [pH], moisture, a food source, poor personal hygiene and poor sanitation) necessary for a food borne illness to survive.

l

- biological (e.g., bacteria or viruses);
- physical (e.g., objects that enter any stage of food preparation); and,
- chemical (e.g., cleaning products and naturally occurring).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to safely dispose of used oils.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Examine safe and responsible recycling and disposal of kitchen waste.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to prepare recipes using proper food safe practices (e.g., frequent hand washing, avoiding food cross-contamination, washing produce, cooking to proper food temperatures).

outcomes.statement:
Demonstrate understanding of SI and imperial units of measurement including:
- linear measurement
- surface area of spheres, and right cones, cylinders, prisms, and pyramids

- relationships between and within measurement systems.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Justify the choice of units and or referents for determining or estimating linear, surface area, or volume measurements in different contexts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the selection of measurement instruments (e.g., rulers, callipers, or tape measures) and the strategies used to determine linear measurements (e.g., circumference of a bottle, length of a curve, or perimeter of the base of an irregular 3-D object).

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f

indicators.text:

items.text: The intent of this course in geography is to acquaint and explain to the student the basic distributions of physical and cultural phenomena over the earth's surface. Through analysis of these distributions, and some of the societal processes, an understanding of the environment, society and economy of the different regions of the world should be achieved. Further, the study of geography should lead to an appreciation of the fact that the world is one, that no region exists in isolation, that, today, all parts of the world are interdependent. To ensure the attainment of the above, the geography program should foster in the student the development of the following understandings, skills, and attitudes:

There is no split between "physical geography" and "regional geography". Geography is a chorological science (i.e., deals with distribution) which needs and uses the facts of many sciences to arrive at an understanding of differences between regions.

Geography is unified by its method and viewpoint and not by its subject matter. Much of its subject matter may be contained in other disciplines -- in history, in physics, in geology, in economics, etc. -- but its viewpoint is distinctive; it is the regional viewpoint.

The regional viewpoint infers the recognition of differences and of similarities between areas across the earth's surface. Regions are distinguished on the basis of definite criteria, both physical and cultural.

Classification of phenomena (physical or cultural) into categories of greater or lesser degree of generalization should lead to the understanding of areal variation in their occurrence and hence to an appreciation of regional distribution.

In recognizing relationships occurring between different classes of phenomena, e.g., areas of dense population coinciding with great natural resources, one must be careful to differentiate between cause and effect relationships and those relationships which are accidental.
The major device for demonstrating regional differences and distributions is the map. In addition the geographer uses a variety of descriptive devices including statistical diagrams of many kinds.
To read with comprehension in the field of geography.
To analyze, interpret and evaluate data provided in many forms (statistical, map, or other).
To discover geographical relationships and to recognize regional differences.
To present, orally and in writing, in organized fashion, the results of geographical research.
To use, and constuct where possible, the various tools of geography including globes, maps, charts, and graphs.
To make case studies, local or other, and thus develop understanding of relationships between environment and human activities.
To undertake geographical studies, including elementary field work, of the local area to achieve first hand under-standing of the fundamental approach of the geographer.
Recognition that the state of knowledge is not finite, that new methods of research and new concepts are continually enolving, that understanding of the world in which we live is very incomplete.
Willingness to undertake research with an open mind and to arrive at generalizations based on unbiased appraisal.
Willingness to recognize that cultural differences across the world are the result of geographical, historical and societal factors rather than a result of "racial" dissimilarities.

A willingness to recognize that regions of similar physical environment may be occupied by very dissimilar economies and societies and that these dissimilarities are a result of numerous factors including stage of cultural and technical development, together with differences in the objectives of the peoples concerned.
A willingness to understand that no region exists in isolation that al1 parts of the world are inter-related and interdependent.

units.name: Unit I: THE PLANET EARTH: ITS CHARACTER AND PORTRAYAL
units.siteUnitName: The Planet Earth: Its Character and Portrayal

items.text: The earth is one of nine planets which revolve around the sun, a relatively small star, and thus forms part of the solar system.
The positions of the moon relative to the earth and sun account for visible variations in its illumination.

The relationships between sun and earth lead to: timing of 24-hour day;the contrasts between day and night; the period of the year; the differences in the amount of solar energy received latitudinally; the seasons; weather and climatic differences; differences in vegetation and soils and thus to differences in agricultural potential and in habitability from region to region.
The spherical shape of the earth necessitates the use of a special system of angular measurements whereby specific locations may be identified.
A system of standard time zones and an International Date Line are necessary in order to avoid confusion in communications.
Different types of map projections are designed to provide accuracy in shape or area, or to provide for a special use (e.g. the Mercator).

units.name: Unit II: THE FORM OF THE EARTH.

items.text: There is a pattern to the earth's structure.
Rocks are classified according to mode of origin and various properties.
The parts of the earth are in a state of balance. When this balance is disturbed, readjustment, the result of internal movements, takes place.
External processes assist in the sculpturing of the earth's surface.
The hydrological cycle refers to the intimate relationships which exist between atmospheric, surface, and sub-surface waters.
Typical landscapes can be associated with specific agents of gradation, and often with typical climates.
Regional landscapes have developed over great periods of time and should be considered in terms of geological time periods.
Variations in weather are the result of frequent changes in the physical characteristics of the atmosphere.
Climate is a generalization of long-term weather conditions.
The elements of climate include temperature, pressure and winds, and precipitation.
Climatic regions of the world are classified according to temperature and precipitation differences.
Regional patterns of natural vegetation are determined largely by regional patterns of climate.
Climate and natural vegetation determine the distribution of the major soil groups

units.name: Unit IV: CLIMATIC REGIONS AND THEIR EFFECTS UPON MAN.
units.siteUnitName: Climatic Regions and Their Effects Upon Man

items.text: Man's activities are closely related to climatic conditions.
The division of the world into climatic regions is based essentially on temperature conditions, with each region subdivided on the basis of rainfal1.
The type of climate in warm temperate lands is determined by the great seasonal shifts of winds and pressure systems that reflect earth-sun relationships.
The westerly winds and the middle-latitude cyclonic disturbances influence the climate of the cool temperate lands. The interiors of these lands are strongly affected by continental air masses.
Polar and arid lands are sparsely populated because of unfavourable climatic conditions.
Climatic "zones" change with altitude as well as with latitude.
Man has utilized each of the climatic regions in particular ways.
Types of farming and agricultural practices are determined by the natural environment, the culture, technology and the objectives of the people.
The demand for and utilization of minerals are determined by the stage of technological development.
The production of hydro-electric power is limited by the factors of water supply, suitable dam sites, and proximity to potential markets.
Transportation facilities are basic to economic progress.
Industrial development is determined by combinations of environmental factors.
Individuals and governments must assume responsibility for the wise use and skillful management of naturalresources.

units.name: Unit VI: P O P UL ATI ON.

items.text: Man has been classified into races-according to physical traits which can be inherited only. NOTE: Emphasize that race is a purely biological term and has no cultural, religious, or linguistic connotations. Further, there is no "pure race".
People of different skin colour and of different cultures often belong to the same race.
There are several theories to account for the distribution of people over the world.
There is an extreme unevenness of distribution of the world population.
World population is increasing rapidly and the problem of supplying the needs of life is becoming more pressing.
Geographical factors tend to control the presence or absence of people in all parts of the world.
Problems of supplying the needs of life arising from overpopulation can be alleviated.
Cities may be classified according to origin, function, and in other ways.

indicators.text: Read and play short (e.g., 2-8 measure) bass riffs or guitar licks.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Read and play one arpeggiated fingerpicking pattern.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Read and play in 4/4 time signature.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Read standard notation to play beginner single note pieces or chords.

outcomes.statement: Examine music theory and how it is used in musical expressions/ideas/compositions.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain time signature and how to count and play in 4/4 time signature.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify beginner rhythmic values in 4/4 time (e.g., quarter note, whole note, half note, eighth note).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify beginner music symbols (e.g., bar line, repeat dots, treble clef).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply, with teacher guidance, aural skills to recreate a short piece.

outcomes.statement: Identify and play guitar music from a variety of cultural and historical contexts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize a range of traditional and contemporary guitar music selections.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore historical information from a variety of cultural and historical contexts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe guitar music from a variety of cultures and periods throughout history.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practise particular genres of music in a stylistically appropriate manner (e.g., genres and styles might include rock, blues, country, classical, fingerstyle, metal, Hawaiian slack key, Celtic, surf, funk, flamenco, r&b/soul, reggae/ska, Brazilian).

outcomes.statement: Explore the lives and work of local, Canadian and international guitar players.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and listen to the work of local, Canadian and international guitar players.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate what makes a guitar player influential.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore how guitar players influence and respond to social, political and cultural issues (e.g., representing gender and sexual diversity, oncern for environmental sustainability or human rights, world music activists).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into how guitar players are influenced throughout their development.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Draw on the experience of local guitar players (e.g., community performances, collaborative workshops, adult musicians, guest artists from diverse cultures) to examine their work and careers and to improve one’s own practice.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research Canadian Indigenous artists whose contemporary guitar music is influenced by traditional Indigenous music.

outcomes.statement: Describe the impact and role of guitar playing in personal life and identify music careers and pathways for continuing engagement in music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the relationship between guitar playing and personal wellness, including mental health (e.g., music therapy, social connection).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the ways that different genres/styles of music influence one’s wellbeing (e.g., mood, anxiety, sense of peace, identity).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore how guitar music is infused in daily life (e.g., to influence consumers via advertising, shopping environments) including media (e.g., film, video games, television, social media, apps).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: List the ways guitar playing can remain part of one’s life beyond school.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize that the sharing of guitar music has evolved throughout history for producers and consumers.

outcomes.statement: Listen to and describe the guitar playing of self and others.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List characteristics of various guitar genres (e.g., rock, country, pop, hip hop).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Use, with teacher guidance, musical terminology when describing guitar playing of self and others (e.g., using the elements of music to describe the guitar playing).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the chords in a song using the harmonized scale.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: List basic characteristics of a guitar player.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Practise ear training while listening (e.g., finding keys).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore live and recorded guitar performances.

outcomes.statement: Design, implement and evaluate, with teacher guidance, a personal practice plan.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a personal inventory to investigate the impact and role of music in one’s own life.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify potential obstacles to practicing and brainstorm possible solutions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify resources (e.g., apps, practice trackers, games, motivation, lessons) to support practice plans.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the elements of effective planning for personal guitar playing growth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Plan the required steps to achieving one’s personal guitar goals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop and use criteria to evaluate one’s own practice plan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Establish one’s own guitar goals and apply the steps necessary to achieve those goals.

outcomes.statement: Listen to and describe ways the guitar is used in contemporary Saskatchewan First Nations and Métis music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to the music of contemporary Saskatchewan First Nations and Métis guitar players and songwriters.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Use, with teacher guidance, musical terminology when describing guitar playing of self and others (e.g., using the elements of music to describe the guitar playing).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: List the characteristics of the guitar playing in First Nations and Métis music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore live and recorded First Nations and Métis guitar performances.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the use of the guitar as an accompanying instrument in Métis fiddle music and kitchen parties.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the skills, techniques and attitudes necessary for successful group performances.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research and discuss creation and production methods used in Western dance (e.g., written text, music, images, choreography) including ownership and copyright.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Play in time with other guitar players.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: List the characteristics of a responsible band member.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create and use own practice plan to improve and prepare for rehearsal.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate leadership as a guitar player (e.g., offering help and guidance to other guitar players in class, being prepared for class).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Participate in class rehearsal discussions when problem solving.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Engage in group playing (e.g., sharing tracks digitally, small groups, large groups).

evidence.observation: The outcomes page groups the outcomes under 9 unit headings.

outcomes.statement: Investigate expectations and standards in the hairstyling and esthetics industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Hairstyling and Esthetics (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify expectations and standards in the hairstyling and esthetics industry such as sanitation, safety, work ethic and professional image.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Construct a list of skills for an individual entering into a career in hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of effective communication such as active listening and speaking clearly as it relates to hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Reflect on the impact of positive and negative non-verbal communication (e.g., smile/frown, body language) when working in the field of hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Define terminology (e.g., draping, sanitization, massage, cuticle, contour) and identify the chosen profession (e.g., hairstyling, nail technician, skin technician, makeup artist) where the term would be used.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research and present on an area of interest found within hairstyling and esthetics (e.g., how much money annually is spent on the beauty industry, how animal testing impacts use of products, the increase in use of environmentally sustainable products).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the question, “How does dermatology, massage therapy, theatrical makeup, hairstyling and barbering fit under the umbrella of the beauty industry?”.

outcomes.statement: Examine general safety requirements within hairstyling and esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: General Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Distinguish between provincial and federal health and safety rules and guidelines as applied to hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify potential hazards in salons, appropriate safety equipment (e.g., personal protective equipment (PPE)) and appropriate safety precautions (e.g., public sanitation, trip hazards).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss general safety practices when using common salon equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Brainstorm general safety guidelines for a salon such as managing wires on the floor, extension cords, walkways and handling chemicals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on the impact that salon cleanliness (e.g., dust, organization) has on safety and business feasibility.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how technician’s choices and behaviours impact safety (e.g., wearing sandals or clothing that exposes skin can cause damage to self or clients).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of ergonomics for the health and well-being of technicians.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the effects that wellness components such as posture, exercise, rest, stress management, hygiene and nutrition have on the success of a hairstylist or esthetician.

outcomes.statement: Justify the importance of proper sanitation, disinfection and sterilization.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Sanitation, Disinfection and Sterilization (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define the terms sanitation, disinfection and sterilization.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the three levels of infection control (i.e., sanitation, disinfection and sterilization).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe contamination and decontamination.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate the purpose and application of antiseptic versus a disinfectant.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Classify given scenarios as sanitizing, disinfecting, or sterilizing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Classify single-use implements versus multi-use tools.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the different levels of disinfection (i.e., high, intermediate and low level) and describe situations when each level is appropriate.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Compare different techniques for sanitizing, disinfecting and sterilizing instruments and surfaces.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate techniques for sanitizing and disinfecting instruments and surfaces.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate different processes for disinfecting, sanitizing and sterilizing non-porous items (e.g., glass, metal, electric files, linen).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Recognize the difference between a chemosterilant and a high level disinfectant.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Compare labels on chemicals for proper use and disposal.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Critique sanitation practices when performing a service (e.g., manicures, pedicure, facial, makeup application, cut and style).

outcomes.statement: Examine general pre- service safety requirements for any salon service.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Pre-service Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss safety precautions when using professional salon products.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain general and specific safety practices for tools used to perform services.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate the process of preparing the workstation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Justify the importance of maintaining a safe and organized workstation throughout a service.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the knowledge and skills necessary to pre-service.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate the process of preparing the client for a service.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate safety knowledge and skills related to pre- service.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss preparations such as appropriate salon documents, client allergies and sensitivities, hair types and textures for given scenarios of upcoming client services.

outcomes.statement: Examine general post- service safety requirements for any salon service.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Post-service Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss safety knowledge and skills related to post-service.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate the post-service safety steps that the stylist/technician performs while the client is in the salon.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe and demonstrate the post-service safety steps that the stylist/technician performs after the client has left the salon.

outcomes.statement: Examine scope of practice within hairstyling and esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Scope of Practice (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify hairstylist services such as shampoo, cut, style and chemically treat hair.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify esthetician services such as massage, skin care, nail enhancements and make up.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Define scope of practice and how it applies to estheticians and hairstylists.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize what is appropriate scope of practice for someone who has not received all the necessary training and certification.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore different steps found within scope of practice (e.g., technician, journeyperson apprentice, journeyperson, medical, dermatologist).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss why hairstylists may also provide services such as scalp treatments, hair additions and barbering techniques.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss why successful hairstylists incorporate technical and interpersonal skills.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate scope of practice within hairstyling and esthetics.

outcomes.statement: Examine professionalism within hairstyling and esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Professionalism (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define professionalism and ethics in the field of hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of a professional image.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how the choices and behaviours of a hairstylist or esthetician impacts their professional lives.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the importance of mental and physical health and well-being for personal and also professional reasons.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Define and compare non-verbal, verbal and written communication.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss qualities of effective communication such as the role of actively listening and confirming expectations of clients.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze the importance of appropriate communication techniques and tools with clients including telephone and technology.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate behaviours (e.g., politeness, accommodating service, modeling hairstyles, nails, make-up and skin) and atmosphere (e.g., music, linens, comfort) that clientele find the most approachable and the most conducive to return business.

outcomes.statement: Examine elements of art and principles of design in hairstyling and esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8A: Elements of Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the elements of art (i.e., colour, form, line, shape, space, texture, tone, value).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the principles of design (i.e., balance, contrast and variety, movement and rhythm, pattern, harmony and unity, emphasis, proportion and scale).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how the elements of art and principles of design apply to artistic expression within the context of hair and esthetics.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Respond critically, using appropriate vocabulary, to examples in the context of hair and esthetics creations considering how the elements of art and principles of design are applied.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Justify why examples of hair and esthetics creations are appealing based on elements of art and principles of design.

outcomes.statement: Examine how beauty can be an expression of a person’s worldview, culture and self-identity.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Inclusive Beauty (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the meaning of worldview, (e.g., attitude and principles) culture (e.g., ethnic background and subculture) and self-identity.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research how techniques and trends in hairstyling and esthetics reflect worldviews, culture and self-identity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine hairstyles, skin care, nail techniques and make-up examples within the local community.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the impact that worldview and culture have on an individual’s definition of beauty.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and discuss historical and current societal attempts to control (e.g., government regulations/intervention, school dress code) self- expression (e.g., significance of the braid) of beauty.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore ideals of beauty (e.g., size of earlobes, length of hair, piercings, length of nails and gender expression) across cultures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the question, how does an individual’s expression of human beauty reflect their worldview, culture or self-identity?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal aesthetic choices (e.g., makeup, hair, nails) and their potential to communicate worldview, culture or self-identity.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how a traditional Western definition of beauty (e.g., hair texture, light-coloured eyes and skin, hetero normativity) excludes and marginalizes expression of identity and culture.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss how cultures that have been historically excluded and marginalized are challenging the stereotypical Western ideal of beauty.

outcomes.statement: Analyze career opportunities within hairstyling and esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Career Opportunities (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Classify different community business options in hairstyling and esthetics including nail technician, make-up artist and skin care technician.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the various career opportunities within the hairstyling and esthetics industry (e.g., hairstylists, hair salons, spas, barber shops, schools, hair replacement clinics, health care establishments, hotels, tourism, fashion and entertainment industries).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore career advancement opportunities in the hairstyling and esthetics industry such as salon managers, salon owners, fashion consultants, educators, platform artists and product sales representatives.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss ways hairstylists may be remunerated such as salary, commission, a combination of salary and commission or chair rental agreements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Interview a community member in a specific field within hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how different careers within hairstyling and esthetics complement one another and how often professionals have more than one trade or certification.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Critique different business examples in the field of hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the qualities (e.g., positive client relationships) of successful technicians.

outcomes.statement: Examine characteristics of a successful salon.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11A: Introduction to Salon (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify relevant laws, regulations and regulatory bodies for a salon that contains hairstyling and esthetics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify procedures for equipment storage, cleaning and organization in a salon.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how a salon can ensure safe and productive work practices.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Categorize components that are necessary for business operation of a successful salon (e.g., operation expenses, working environment, profit margin, ethics and client relationships).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research accurate client-scheduling skills including allowing sufficient time for all treatments and services.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe skills salon employees need to recommend and sell products and services.

outcomes.statement: Explore the scope of technicians in esthetics.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Introduction to Esthetics (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify different treatments performed by skin and nail technicians.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research tools, equipment and maintenance used in esthetics.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how technicians can ensure safe and productive work practices including employing proper ergonomics and personal protective equipment (PPE) throughout services.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how advancements in technology have impacted esthetics.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the consultation process and its impact on the client’s experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Client Consultation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify communications skills such as asking clarifying questions used in successful client consultations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a list of possible questions for client consultations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how respect for a client’s worldview, culture or self-identity should inform the consultation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Critique appropriate communication skills during a client consultation scenario or within a classroom role play.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss preparations for client consultation such as appropriate salon documents, client allergies and sensitivities, hair textures (e.g., fine, medium, coarse, kinky and curl pattern) and hair characteristics (e.g., density, porosity, elasticity).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine, through client consultation scenarios, the type of service, the required time and the total cost.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the question, how important is the client consultation for a successful salon experience?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss how technicians can create an inclusive and welcoming environment for all clients, including the important role language plays in client experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain the importance of confirming the final outcome for the service.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify ways to establish, document, maintain and store records of client services/treatments.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate discretion and confidentiality in acquiring and managing client information.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Analyze examples (e.g., potential bias, gender normativity expectations) that could negatively impact the client consultation process.

outcomes.statement: Explore hairstyling and esthetics products.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: General Product Knowledge (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define categories such as professional, prestige and drugstore as used to distinguish hairstyling and esthetics products.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the questions: What can certain products offer that others cannot? Why would professionals want to use professional products?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of licensed sellers when purchasing hairstyling and esthetics products.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the qualifications required to work for a licensed seller or within hairstyling and esthetics product distribution.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the reason qualifications are beneficial for those employed within product distribution.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze different products, including following manufacturer’s instructions, to optimize results.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Justify product selection for provided scenarios (e.g., client has a certain skin type, hair texture or desires a specific outcome).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine ingredients used in products (e.g., consumer packaging and labelling act and regulations for Canada) and the potential impact on the health of clients.

outcomes.statement: Analyze hair care products.

indicators.text: Categorize different hair care products based on their chemical ingredients or lack of chemical ingredients.

indicators.text: Determine the pH level of hair and products (e.g., shampoos, conditioners, hydrochloric acid, lye, permanent wave solution).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss what impact drugstore products have on hair compared to professional hair care products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare ingredient lists of professional products for different hair textures and characteristics.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize how allergies and conditions affect product selection.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the question, how does hair texture (e.g., fine, medium, coarse, kinky, curl pattern or coil configuration) and hair characteristics (e.g., elasticity, porosity, condition and density) influence the selection of hair care products?

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the environmental impact and sustainability of products and packaging.

outcomes.statement: Analyze skin care products.

indicators.text: Identify skin care products and discuss criteria for selection based on alignment with client budget and behaviours (e.g., work outside, stay at home and little or ongoing application of makeup).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare drugstore products to professional products.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare ingredient lists of professional products for different skin types.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize how allergies and conditions (e.g., pregnancy) could affect product selection.

indicators.text: Investigate what ingredients give products their shelf life.

indicators.text: Define potential hydrogen (pH), acidity and alkalinity.

indicators.text: Describe procedures for application and removal of skin care products such as cleansers, toners, masks, serums and moisturizers.

indicators.text: Identify contraindications and how it could affect skin care product selection.

indicators.text: Define and examine hypoallergenic products.

indicators.text: Determine the maintenance and storage of products used for skin care.

indicators.text: Respond critically, referencing ingredients and expectations presented, to marketing strategies (e.g., targeting demographics, filters) used to sell skin care products.

outcomes.statement: Analyze makeup products.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14D: Makeup Product Knowledge (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify different makeup products (e.g., foundation, concealer, powder, eyeshadow, eyeliner, mascara, lashes, blush, contour, eyebrow and lip products) used in creating a full make up look.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the different formulations of makeup products such as liquid, cream, gel, mousse, cake, loose powder, pressed powder.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify all of the different packaging options for cosmetics (e.g., wand and liquid products, crème or gel based products, loose powder, pressed powder, pencils, stick products) and discuss how to safely use each.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain appropriate kit maintenance including cleaning products and brushes before and after use.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Categorize makeup products and discuss criteria for selection based on alignment with client budget and behaviours (e.g., work outside, stay at home and little or ongoing application of makeup).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare drugstore makeup products to professional products.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare ingredient lists of professional products.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recognize how allergies affect makeup product selection.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research the environmental impact and sustainability of makeup products and packaging.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate what ingredients give products their shelf life.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Determine the maintenance and storage of products used in makeup.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine ingredients used in products (e.g., consumer packaging and labelling act and regulations for Canada) and the potential impact on the health of clients.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Discuss what makeup products can achieve compared to the use of technology (e.g., filter, photoshop).

outcomes.statement: Examine nail care products.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15A: Nail Product Knowledge (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a list of the products used during nail care treatments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine and describe products used for various nail care treatments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify nail care treatment products that require protective equipment (PPE).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Distinguish nail care products classified as prohibited, restricted, or controlled.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine the maintenance, storage and safe disposal of products and consumable items used in nail care.

outcomes.statement: Examine maintenance and use of hairstyling equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16A: Hair Styling Equipment and Maintenance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify single-use and multi-use manual tools, styling tools, cutting tools, electric tools, chemical service tools and equipment used in hairstyling.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how manual tools, electric tools and equipment are used in hairstyling.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate application of hairstyling manual tools, electric tools and equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize how proper ergonomic practices are necessary to maintain the health of stylists.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of sanitation and safety for each tool and piece of equipment used in hairstyling.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe and perform sanitization, sterilization or disinfection of tools and equipment (e.g., spraying disinfectant, wiping and soaking; handling/storing cleaning towels, capes, aprons and smocks).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe and perform an inspection process (e.g., check for product build- up and determine when a tool must be removed from service) to maintain manual tools, electric tools and equipment (e.g., remove debris from filters in hairdryers, clippers and clothes dryer and discard refuse and product waste according to regulations).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss and apply safety practises when using all tools and equipment (e.g., adjust hydraulic chairs and other equipment according to stylist’s ergonomic support, use personal protective equipment (PPE), locate first aid and eye wash stations, discard sharps according to regulations and recognize all hazards).

outcomes.statement: Examine characteristics of hair and scalp.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17A: Hair and Scalp (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify hair structures (i.e., cuticle, cortex and medulla) and sub-scalp structures (e.g., hair root and gland systems).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Summarize factors that affect hair growth such as age, nutrition, health and hormones.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Determine hair texture (e.g., fine, medium, coarse, kinky and curl pattern) and characteristics such as weight, shape, elasticity, porosity, density and growth patterns.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore techniques (e.g., stretch single hair, feel hair with hands) used to determine elasticity and porosity.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize effects on hair exhibiting a lack of moisture or protein.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform hair analysis and recommend products for maintenance, optimal health and condition of hair.

outcomes.statement: Execute a shampoo and condition tailored to a client’s needs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Shampoo and Rinse (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss with client their current hair care needs and concerns.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze hair to determine which shampoo and conditioner would be suitable for the client.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Experiment with appropriate conditions (e.g., water temperature, detangling techniques, brush and comb selection and water nozzle distance) for washing hair.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practice proper scalp manipulations and techniques for shampooing and conditioning hair and scalp.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform pre-brushing, draping, shampoo (e.g., apply, lather, appropriate pressure to suit client ensuring complete saturation) and conditioner (e.g., ensure hydration, close the cuticle and detangle).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss and apply sanitary procedures when shampooing hair.

outcomes.statement: Investigate hair styles and hair styling techniques.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19A: Hair Styling (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 9, 14B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify styling aid (e.g., mousse, serum and spray) selection and application needed to achieve desired finish.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine language used in hairstyling to describe hair textures (e.g., fine, medium, coarse, kinky and curl pattern) and hair characteristics (e.g., elasticity, porosity and density).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of using appropriate industry terminology when describing hair by referencing texture (e.g., fine, medium, coarse, kinky and curl pattern) and characteristics (density, elasticity, porosity).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine and apply different hair styles (e.g., weaving, knotting, locs, box braids and twists).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Execute braiding techniques including visible, invisible and fishtail.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the significance of braiding in First Nations’ cultures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform and critique a roller set and comb-out.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate finger waving and pin-curl technique.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform and critique blow-dry and curling iron techniques.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss and apply appropriate safety measures when using a blow dryer or a curling iron.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Construct a design plan for implementing thermal tools.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Implement elements of art and principles of design, use of tools, hair terminology and safety to achieve a selected look from a visual support (e.g., picture, video, other technology supports).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the questions, how does hair styling impact an individual’s self-esteem and well-being or how does a hairstyle reflect an individual’s worldview?

outcomes.statement: Examine the function, types, conditions and characteristics of skin.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20A: Introduction to Skin Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and describe the structures (e.g., epidermis and dermis) and functions (e.g., heat regulation, absorption, excretion and sensation) of skin.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine how client’s choices and behaviours (e.g., working outside, sunscreen) may affect skin including factors that might preserve the health of skin.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the nerves of the skin and explain the function of the nerves.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define and explain melanin, types of glands (e.g., oil and sweat), skin disorders and conditions and skin type (e.g., oily and dry).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of steaming/hot towels on the face.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and manipulations of massage.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate the manipulations used in massage.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a facial.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain and demonstrate the use of equipment, implements, products and materials when giving a facial.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Practice appropriate safety and sanitation procedures when conducting skin care services.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the question, how do environmental factors affect the skin?

outcomes.statement: Examine the benefits of performing an analysis of features prior to make up application.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21: Analysis of Features (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze client skin, eyes and hair colour to determine colour/product selection for make up application.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss relevant elements of art and principles of design as it applies to the makeup creation process.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Justify your colour/product selections considering how the elements of art, principles of design and colour theory are applied.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the basics of colour theory as it applies to make up such as blue eyes stand out with bronze shadow.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain basics of chiaroscuro highlight and contour (e.g., light emphasizes and dark minimizes).

outcomes.statement: Analyze a makeup consultation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22: Make Up Consultation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 21

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Brainstorm questions technicians may ask to gather information related to client events (e.g., special occasion, long day/night, prom, wedding), environmental factors and desired look.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss questions that inform technicians about client’s personal taste (e.g., areas that make client self conscious, coordination with clothing and jewelry, type and amount of make up normally worn).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a makeup look based on consultation answers and knowledge gained through the analysis of features.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the importance of a thorough consultation and how that contributes to client satisfaction and repeat business.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Plan and execute a makeup consultation.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with makeup application.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23A: Make Up Application (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify types of tools used for makeup application (e.g., brush and sponge) and the cleaning and maintenance for each (e.g., single use disposable and reusable tools that can be cleaned and sterilized).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify different varieties of makeup products and what they are used for or best suited to.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Execute a variety of make up looks using the correct tools and products on people or on models (e.g., face plate, watercolour paper).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a makeup look from a visual support (e.g., picture, video, technology and social media) or from a live demonstration from a qualified professional.

outcomes.statement: Examine the nail and influences on nail health.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24: Introduction to Nail Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the composition and technical name for the nail.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the composition and the appearance of a healthy nail.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the purpose of nails.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define keratin and discuss the importance to nail health and growth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the average growth of the nail and factors that influence nail growth and health.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how the shape of the matrix influences the shape of the natural nail.

outcomes.statement: Explore the structure of the nail.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Nail Structure (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the parts of the nail.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the structures associated with the nail (e.g., nail plate, nail bed, matrix, lunula, cuticle, eponychium, hyponychium, nail wall, nail groove and free edge).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and explain the structures beneath the nail, the skin surrounding the nail and the composition of the nail plate.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine safe treatment of the various parts/structures of the nail.

outcomes.statement: Examine multi-use equipment and implements used for manicures.

indicators.text: Describe multi-use equipment and implements used during various manicure services.

indicators.label: b

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f

outcomes.statement: Examine single-use equipment and implements used for manicures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26B: Manicure Single-Use Equipment and Implements (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe single-use equipment and implements used during various manicure services.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the safe operation, maintenance and storage of single-use equipment and implements used during a manicure service.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Distinguish the difference between multi-use equipment and implements and single-use materials and supplies.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the need for personal protective equipment (PPE) when using single-use equipment and implements for manicure treatments.

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate discretion and confidentiality in acquiring and managing client information.

indicators.text: Create a list of questions to include on a client intake/consultation form (e.g., current health issues, medications, allergies and sensitivities and requested services).

indicators.label: l

items.stem: The knowledge objectives are to help students:
items.heading: Foundational Objectives for the Course Social Organizations

items.stem: The skills/abilities objectives are to help students:

items.heading: Foundational Objectives for the Course Social Organizations

items.stem: The values objectives are to help students:
items.heading: Foundational Objectives for the Course Social Organizations

items.text: Know that humans establish various kinds of organizations as a means of systematically meeting their needs and wants.
Know that in order to have security, stability, and predictability, humans tacitly agree to conform to the beliefs, values, and mores imposed on them by the various organizations of society.
Know that any group or organization must decide on some means of decision making that will allow it to function effectively.
Know that groups or organizations must have some way of resolving differences and making and enforcing conclusions so that a collective course of action can be carried out.
Review/learn the skill of categorizing and classifying material according to some system in order to make it meaningful.
Review/learn the skill of drawing inferences from the patterns that emerge from classification systems.
Review/learn the use of criteria as a basis for analysing an event or situation.
Learn the skill of hypothesizing.
Learn to test hypotheses against historical fact.
What are legitimate constraints on human behaviour?
Should the rights of the individual or the group have the higher priority?
What areas of life are appropriate for society to control, through norms and sanctions?
Should some people be given more power and privilege than others?
Should men and women be given the same access to power and privileges?
Is the use of force ever justified in a conflict over social change?
Know that a study of history may be helpful in relating the cumulative human experience of the past to our experiences with reality.
Know that historical events can be chronologically ordered.
Know some of the major events and dates of chronological world history.
Know that an accurate description of "what has occurred where" is fundamental to an interpretation of why these events have occurred.
Know the geographic location of the major places which play a role in the history of this course.
Review the skill of organizing information for analysis.
Practise making generalizations and drawing inferences from classified data.
Practise map interpretation.
Does one's culture influence what is perceived to be a major historical event?
Know that human beings live in society because they can best satisfy their needs and wants by working with other members of society.
Know that social organizations stem from and deal with the basic, universal problems of ordered, social life.
Know that social organizations provide for the needs and wants of Canadians, provide them with meaning and purpose, and give them direction and discipline.
Know that social organizations play a significant role in providing order and direction within a society.
Know that social organizations establish norms or values which legitimize sanctions used to regulate human behaviour.
Know that the regulations of social organizations discipline human behaviour to conform to some definite, continuous, and organized patterns of behaviour.
Know that the freedom to live one's life according to the dictates of one's conscience is a significant value in Canadian society.
Know that social organizations based on the cultural assumptions of one historical tradition may be quite different from the social organizations based on another cultural tradition.
Learn to use their own background knowledge as a source of useful data for understanding concepts.
Review/teach the skills of brainstorming and exchanging information through class discussions.
Learn to use grids as a way of organizing information for analysis.
(See activity guide.)
Review/teach the skill of categorizing material according to some system in order to make it meaningful.
Should social organizations be able to use sanctions to control and direct human behaviour?
Should limits be placed on this power?
Should conformity take precedence over individualism?
Know that the established organizations people live within are part of their cultural heritage.
Know that pluralism is the belief that groups which are distinctly unique should have that distinctiveness recognized and protected.
Know that the basic assumptions on which social organizations are organized come from the prevailing world view.
Know that organizations established by one cultural group in Canada may based on very different values than those established by another cultural group.
Know that organizations establish a system of persons or things ranked one above the other.
Know that women should have the same opportunities within society as men.
Practise using their own background knowledge as a source of useful data for understanding concepts.
Practise the skills of brainstorming and exchanging information through class discussions.
Practise using concepts as criteria for making evaluations.
Would they (the students) wish to live in a world without morality, ethics, or values?
Would a world where people had no constraints on their behaviour be one that you would want to live in?
Should the rights of the individual or the rights of the group have the higher priority?
What areas of life is it appropriate for society to control through norms and sanctions?
Know that a social contract is an agreement between the rulers and the ruled which defines the rights and duties of each explicitly and implicitly.
Know that each social organization will determine its particular purpose, a set of beliefs and values, and an organization and structure which will include a decision making system.
Know that political decision making occurs in every social organization in an attempt to reconcile the different needs and wants within the organization.
Know that societies have to make decisions about how best to reconcile the conflicting interests within society.
Know that politics is the process of conciliating individuals and groups by giving them a share of valued scarce resources according to the amount of power they wield within society.

Know that power may be expressed through:
- the use of force;
