outcomes.statement: Develop and implement effective management strategies that can be applied to a variety of tasks.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Task Management (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Consider and describe the purpose, target audience and desired outcome of a task or project.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Produce a project according to the plan.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Proofread and critique a product.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Solicit feedback from other interested parties.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Edit and revise a product.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Submit a finished product to its intended audience.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Determine whether or not the desired outcome of the task was achieved.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect on one’s management strategies and their effectiveness in completing a specific task.

outcomes.statement: Explore the use of information processing technologies in various career paths.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Information Processing in the Workplace (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the application of information processing technologies in various sectors (e.g., agriculture, business, life management, communication, resource management, construction, manufacturing and transportation).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the options and opportunities that are available for education and training in the use of information processing technologies beyond the school setting.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Interview individuals regarding their use of information processing technologies in the workplace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how the evolution of information processing technologies has changed the workplace in the past, and predict how it might continue to create change in the future.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss gender stereotypes that exist in information processing careers.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate transferrable skills needed in careers (e.g., punctuality, time management, communication, interpersonal relations).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Consider how diversity (e.g., language, culture, ability, mobility) in the workplace might be accommodated through the use of information processing technologies.

outcomes.statement: Explain various perspectives about what it means to be a positive digital citizen.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Digital Citizenship A (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the characteristics of a positive digital citizen.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain concepts related to copyright such as fair use, creative commons, plagiarism and theft.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the ethics and legality of using e-commerce technology (e.g., online banking, retail websites, social media forums) to purchase or sell items.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the importance of maintaining a positive digital presence.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain how one’s actions might impact one’s digital identity.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the concept of one’s digital footprint with respect to the permanent nature of online actions and communications.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize the effects of a digital presence on individual physical and mental health and well-being (e.g., loneliness, self-esteem).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate respect for diversity (e.g., language, culture, ability, mobility, gender and sexual diversity) when communicating or interacting with others online.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the rights and responsibilities of a digital citizen.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4B: Digital Citizenship B (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain that there is interconnectedness between thoughts and actions which is based on the implied and explicit intention of those actions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and critique the rights and responsibilities of individuals and institutions associated with being a digital citizen.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine classroom, school and school division technology use policies and analyze the consequences of non-compliance.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why technology use policies exist in schools and in businesses.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare classroom, school and school division technology use policies with the rights and responsibilities of a digital citizen and speculate on the reasons for similarities and differences.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how matters such as digital surveillance, data collection and mining and permanence of information on the Internet relate to personal rights and privacy issues.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Justify when a digital citizen’s ethical responsibilities supersede one’s digital rights (e.g., students have the right to freedom of expression online, but ethical responsibilities prohibit them from bullying online or posting explicit images or photographs without consent).

outcomes.statement: Describe and demonstrate the effective use of digital communication.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5A: Digital Communication A (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and use communication platforms such as email and social media for a variety of purposes such as managing and sharing information, connecting with others and displaying learning.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Critique various social media platforms and explain how their utilization may impact one’s digital reputation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify features such as logical (Boolean) operators and filters and describe the advantages of using them when performing internet searches.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Explain the opportunities, limitations and implications of using online tools such as cloud computing, online learning platforms and file sharing to share documents and work collaboratively.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Utilize online tools such as cloud computing, online learning platforms and file sharing to share a variety of documents, including word processing documents, presentations and PDF files.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the impact of using anonymous posting apps and apps that have features such as “disappearing” posts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss online gaming as a form of digital communication.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Create a strategy for the inclusion of appropriate language, content, and images reflective of societal and legal standards in personal, classroom and school digital projects and assignments.

outcomes.statement: Investigate legal and ethical aspects of online interactions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: Digital Law A (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify conventional practices (e.g., including the file path for a URL, citing the source) for sharing content, such as downloading video and posting images of others, in digital environments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits and limitations of user authentication techniques to prevent or allow access to resources.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the concept of Open Content (Creative Commons) licensing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Search for online Open Content images and name their sources.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Conduct a reverse image search to find the source of an image.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Construct citations for sources of online information, including digital media.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine laws surrounding online interactions, including using information and downloading and sharing digital media.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide examples of laws that have emerged or evolved because of changes in the digital world (e.g., illegal file sharing, sharing of intimate photographs without consent).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize that laws change in response to emerging issues with online communication.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain that the social, cultural, economic, and political conditions of the past played and continue to play a significant role in both the reality of the present and the reality they have yet to shape.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Assess one’s behaviours and practices with respect to ethics and laws surrounding online interactions.

outcomes.statement: Recognize and demonstrate proper ergonomic and touch keyboarding techniques.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Keyboarding A (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and demonstrate proper keyboarding ergonomics (e.g., sitting position, keyboard placement, hand position, mouse placement).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Define repetitive strain injury (RSI).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how proper ergonomics relate to injury prevention.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Take regular movement and stretch breaks.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain proper ergonomics specific to different devices (e.g., cellular phone, tablet, laptop).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare ergonomic practices when typing on devices such as cellular phones and tablets to keyboarding on a traditional computer keyboard.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate keyboarding using the designated fingering of the correct hand (e.g., alphabetic keys, numeric keys, symbols).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Use function keys for performing actions (e.g., undo, redo, close, save, print).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify “shift” and “ctrl” modifier key shortcuts for performing actions (e.g., capitalize, undo, cut, copy, paste).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Type with a speed and accuracy of approximately 30 correct words per minute.

outcomes.statement: Design and produce a variety of written documents using a word processing application, following conventional formatting standards.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8A: Word Processing A (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain why word processor applications are used to produce a variety of documents (e.g., letters, résumés, reports, posters).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Use keyboard shortcuts when performing simple actions such as printing, copying, pasting and undoing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use basic formatting (e.g., page layout, fonts, tabs, alignment) to configure a document.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with the inclusion of graphic elements (e.g., text boxes, graphics, lines, shapes) to refine a document.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select and apply conventionally accepted formatting for various documents (e.g., one-page reports, letters, informational brochures, résumés).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Construct a multi-page document incorporating components such as title page, pagination and reference page.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Select and apply appropriate printer options for various tasks.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of editing tools such as spell and grammar check, thesaurus, track changes and proofreaders’ marks.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply basic electronic file management practices to organize information (e.g., save location, naming files).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Use a collaborative online word processing application to edit a document.

outcomes.statement: Apply key concepts and basic elements of computer technology to daily operations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Computer Technology A (Core) · Suggested Time: 1-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and manage basic computer hardware components (e.g., power switches, cable connections, power sources).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify differences between common input/output (I/O) connectors (e.g., USB-A, USB-B, USB-C, Mini-USB, Micro-USB, USB-3, VGA, DVI, HDMI, DisplayPort, 3.5 mm audio, Ethernet, SATA).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use hardware and applications responsibly and effectively.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize elements (e.g., hardware, software, mobile applications, technology networks) that allow for effective use of computer technology.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the role of typical hardware (e.g., CPU, wireless card, RAM, graphics card, SIM card, hard drive and motherboard) found within computing devices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Use proper terminology (e.g., icon, window, menus, scroll) related to computer technology.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Manipulate screen or desktop properties and accessibility options such as sounds, backgrounds, and text size.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply effective file management practices (e.g., storage, creating folders, naming conventions).

outcomes.statement: Assess the impact of computer technology on society, including its prevalence in our everyday lives.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9B: Computer Technology B (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 9A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize various hardware such as tablets, smart phones and laptops, as computing devices.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate changes in computer technologies (e.g., smart phones, laptops, mobile applications) over time.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare computer-assisted operations (e.g., word processing, sending text messages, internet searches) with the equivalent operations from 25, 50 or 75 years ago.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the societal impacts of computer technologies such as digital assistants, social media applications, global connections and working remotely, augmented reality, virtual reality and mixed reality.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify how variations in access to computer technology might create inequities between students within a school, one school compared to another, and one community (e.g., remote location with intermittent internet service) compared to another (urban location with latest technology for internet access).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain why a country with a developing economy and extreme geographical terrain may face challenges related to the infrastructure required to make technologies accessible to its citizens.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the environmental impacts of the manufacture, use, and disposal of some computing devices (e.g., the use of heavy metals in manufacturing, disposable devices).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify and discuss the utility of computer related products that are currently on the market (e.g., smart appliances and home automation, augmented, mixed and virtual reality applications, smartphones, Global Positioning Systems and self-driving vehicles).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect on the importance of computer technology in one’s life by asking questions such as: What would I do differently without my mobile device?; In what ways is society reliant on computers?

outcomes.statement: Investigate various operating systems in computing devices, and describe and apply their attributes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Operating Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 9B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define the term operating system, and describe the role of an operating system in a computing device.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the strengths and limitations of various operating systems, including Android, iOS, Windows, MacOS and Linux.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a server and the role of a server in using a computer remotely.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify operating system functions (e.g., running applications, configuring peripherals, organizing files) that meet various user needs.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Organize and manage files (e.g., copy, move, delete, rename, create shortcut).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate and apply conventional procedures to back up and archive user files.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze differences between various cloud storage methods.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify when it is more appropriate to use a server and when it is more appropriate to use a personal computer for file storage.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain considerations related to the purchase of operating systems, including purpose, necessity and cost.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess user computing needs and select an appropriate operating system for different scenarios (e.g., a student on a fixed budget, a gamer, a photographer).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the purpose and characteristics of spreadsheets.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Provide a definition for the term spreadsheet.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the purpose, benefits and limitations of spreadsheets.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss practical uses for spreadsheets.

indicators.text: Explore formatting options available in spreadsheets, including row height, column width, borders, numerical formats, alignments and fills.

outcomes.statement: Explain and use the mathematical features that are characteristic of spreadsheet applications.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15B: Spreadsheets B (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 15A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the mathematical concept of order of operations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform calculations in spreadsheets using simple mathematical formulae that include addition (+), subtraction (-), division (/), multiplication (*) and exponentiation (^).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain that a function is a pre-defined formula.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply introductory mathematical functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MAX, MIN and ROUND to perform calculations in spreadsheets.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare the effectiveness of the fill handle to that of copying and pasting when replicating and adapting data.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare the efficiency of using mathematical functions to developing mathematical formulas from scratch.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the effects of changing one or several data values in spreadsheets.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss how data within a spreadsheet can be used to facilitate the decision-making process.

outcomes.statement: Create and manipulate spreadsheets using a variety of functions and formats for various purposes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15C: Spreadsheets C (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 15B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate basic data entry and manipulation in spreadsheets.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the benefits of a separate number pad when working in a spreadsheet program.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Generate spreadsheets that contain cells with all three types of information (label, value, formula) to build documents such as invoices, gradebooks or scoresheets.

indicators.label: d
e
f
indicators.text: Identify common error values (e.g., ######error, #Name?error, #VALUE!error, #REF!error) and how to fix them.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate between absolute and relative cell references.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how an IF function can be used to solve a problem on a spreadsheet.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Compare characteristics of different views (e.g., print view, frozen panes) of a spreadsheet.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Change the print orientation and margins of a worksheet for optimal viewing and information retrieval.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Print a specific set of cells or a segment of a worksheet.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Perform actions such as printing, copying, pasting and undoing, using keyboard shortcuts.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the purpose and characteristics of databases.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16A: Databases A (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and function of a variety of filing systems (e.g., alphabetical, numerical, Dewey Decimal).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of a database.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Provide examples of how and where databases are used.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss various types of database systems and architectures, such as relational, graph and flat file databases.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the differences in features and capabilities between databases and spreadsheets and discuss when one application would be preferable to the other.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Define standard terminology associated with database management applications software, including field, record, data type, forms, views, tables, primary key, query, filter.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics and features of a database, including fields, records, data types, forms, views, tables, primary keys, queries, filters.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply simple filters and queries to a given database in order to search and display records that meet given criteria.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Preview and print a datasheet.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Compare the features and functionality of various database software and mobile apps.

outcomes.statement: Produce a variety of technically high quality photographs using digital camera technology.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17A: Digital Photography A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss issues related to digital photography, including the concept of reasonable expectation of privacy, the ethics of image manipulation, tagging, and the ownership of digital images as it pertains to photography.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the roles and purposes of digital photography in society, including personal, professional and commercial uses.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the location and function of the parts and controls of digital cameras (e.g., body, lens, battery, storage media, power switch, shutter release, menu button, shortcut keys).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the functions, parts and controls of digital cameras to those of other mobile image-input devices.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the technical quality of a variety of photographs.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Define and apply criteria for choosing shooting locations, with consideration for safety, background and lighting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify typical automatic, semi-automatic and manual shooting modes on digital cameras and discuss reasons for choosing one mode over another.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the photographic effects of the three settings (e.g., shutter speed, aperture and ISO) of the exposure triangle.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Shoot a variety of photographs that demonstrate technical quality, using a digital camera such as a single lens reflex or a mobile device.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Critique the technical quality of one’s own and others’ photographs, using criteria one has developed.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore computer software and hardware options for organization and storage of photographs.

outcomes.statement: Produce a variety of photographs that exemplify creative composition.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17B: Digital Photography B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 17A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Appraise the use of creative composition in a variety of photographs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Categorize a variety of photographs by genre (e.g., landscape, still life, people).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Shoot photographs that demonstrate a variety of standard framing compositions, including wide, long, full, ¾, medium, head and shoulders, close up and extreme close up.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Shoot photographs using a variety of standard camera angles, including eye level, high angle, low angle, point of view and over the shoulder.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify standard rules of composition, including the rule of thirds, focal point, framing, cropping, leading lines, fore/middle/background and balance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Experiment with creative composition techniques by adjusting focus, shutter speed, depth and pattern.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Shoot a variety of photographs that demonstrate creative composition, using a digital camera such as a single lens reflex or a mobile device.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop criteria to assess creative composition in photographs.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the creative composition of one’s own and others’ photographs.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Sort and manage a collection of photographs using computer software.

outcomes.statement: Improve the appearance and usefulness of digital photographs through the use of retouching applications.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17C: Digital Photography C (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 17B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Assess the relative advantages and disadvantages of applications (e.g., online websites, desktop software, mobile apps) for retouching digital photographic images.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the social and cultural implications of the use of retouched images in the media (e.g., visual misrepresentations of reality or conventional depictions of beauty).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ethical and copyright considerations in relation to the use of others’ images.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why one might choose to purchase stock photography rather than using one’s own photographs.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Critique the technical quality and composition of a photograph and identify characteristics that could be improved through retouching.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of standard tools (e.g., crop, exposure, contrast, saturation, highlights and shadows, white balance, colour adjustments, detail) used in retouching applications.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective retouching of a variety of photographs.

outcomes.statement: Produce a variety of short video clips demonstrating high quality, creative camera operation, using digital video camera technology.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18A: Video Production A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 17A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the concept of reasonable expectation of privacy as it pertains to video creation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the roles and purposes of video production in society, including personal, professional and commercial uses.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the potential purposes, requirements and properties of a recorded video production to those of a live-streamed video.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the technical quality of a specific video.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Appraise the use of creative composition in a specific video.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the function and location of the parts and controls of digital video cameras (e.g., body, lens, battery, storage media, power switch, record button, zoom).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare the functions, parts and controls of digital video cameras to those of mobile device cameras.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the importance of using a tripod when shooting video and demonstrate its effective use while shooting.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify and implement criteria for shooting locations, including safety, background, lighting and acoustics.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text:
Shoot a variety of short video clips that demonstrate technical quality and creative composition, and that include the following:
- standard composition shots (wide, long, full, ¾, medium, head and shoulders, close up, extreme close up);
- standard camera angles (eye level, high angle, low angle, point of view, over the shoulder); and,
- standard camera movements (tilt, pan, zoom, dolly).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Critique the quality of video clips according to established criteria and determine what can be used in post-production and what needs to be rerecorded.

outcomes.statement: Consolidate multiple media clips to create one video, using video editing software.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18B: Video Production B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Determine the purpose and intended audience for a video production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss ethics and copyright in relation to the use of others’ content in video production.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of different software and hardware applications and configurations for editing video.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Critique the quality and appropriateness of media assets (e.g., video clips, photographs, audio files, graphics) for inclusion in a video project.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Import and organize media assets into video editing software.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Arrange media assets on the timeline with appropriately chosen “in” and “out” points and cuts to achieve appropriate pacing of the video.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the nature of jump cuts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Insert post-production components such as sound effects, graphics, titles and transitions on the video timeline.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Export video projects using export settings (codec) that are appropriate for the intended audience and usage.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Critique the finished video according to established criteria.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss the logistical and legal implications of using online video distribution platforms to share content.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Consider video quality, compression and file sizes when planning for publication.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Publish the video for presentation to the intended audience.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and apply basic concepts of graphic design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Introduction to Graphic Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine how the readability of typography is determined by factors such as typeface, font size, style, serif and spacing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and explore components of engaging graphic layout for a variety of digital formats.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Critique examples of layout in graphic design, considering concepts such as weight of elements, use of white space, balance, focus and flow.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the role of colour in graphic design, such as evoking emotion or conveying the spirit and intent of the message.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply various design elements such as line, shape, texture, space, colour and form, and explain the choices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Experiment with various principles of composition such as balance, emphasis, rhythm, movement, variety and harmony.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate consistent use of graphic design components (e.g., font, colour, background) within a project.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply basic concepts of graphic design to the creation of a document such as a magazine or book cover, logo, poster or multimedia presentation, and justify the choice of graphic design elements.

outcomes.statement: Create a presentation which includes a variety of presentation software design elements.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Presentation Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Determine when the use of presentation software is more effective than another medium such as a print document.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore various software and programs used in the production of presentations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and explain various elements (e.g., special effects, animations, sound) of presentation software.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Critique examples of presentations according to principles of graphic design (e.g., quality of pictures, use of colour, size of text).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create and apply presentation templates.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Construct an effective presentation that includes a variety of design elements (e.g., text, shapes, drawing, photographs, audio, video, hyperlinks).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Control the flow of a multimedia presentation using object animations, slide transitions and timing.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Justify the selection of particular design elements within a presentation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Publish a presentation to the Web.

outcomes.statement: Critique a variety of websites to assess their appropriateness and their effectiveness for the intended audience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21A: Website Design A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 19 and 20

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Locate websites in a topic area of interest.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine and assess the design and visual impact of a variety of websites.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Hypothesize about the intended audience of various websites, and provide reasons for the hypothesis.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify elements that hold viewers’ interests in a variety of websites.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate web accessibility (e.g., visual, auditory, language, navigation) in various websites.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Contemplate the role of community standards (e.g., legal parameters, ethical boundaries, norms and values) and cultural awareness in website design.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Locate examples of websites that exemplify current community standards in relation to sexism, racism, ageism, and genderism, and describe how each is an exemplary model.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify potential concerns of immediate nature, such as personal safety, reputation and legal responsibility, and longer term consequences, such as permanence of digital legacy, associated with posting of images or comments on websites.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate and articulate legal issues such as copyright, privacy and consent related to website design.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss factors that make a website effective in conveyance of intended purpose, including content placement, structure, scope and sequence, graphics and appearance, and navigation and usability.

outcomes.statement: Create original digital images using an image editing tool.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22A: Digital Images A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 19

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create an artistic, engaging composition using a digital image editing tool.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Use various hardware (e.g., tracking ball, stylus, mouse, touch screen) to become familiar with the feel and control of digital canvas tools in editing software.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply a range of fill techniques, including pencil, paint brush, spray can, spot, whole fill, and partial fill, to add dimension to digital images.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Sketch and shade a variety of forms using various digital imaging tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Experiment with the digital editing tools to create optical effects such as soft shading, fading, monochromatic, hard shading and motion.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Use digital editing tools to add detail to compositions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate between raster and vector images and explain when one image is preferred over the other.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Differentiate among the uses of different digital graphics formats (e.g., jpegs, gifs, png, bmp) and apply to images as appropriate.

evidence.quote: All PAA curricula are designed using modules, each with a single outcome for students to achieve.

allEvidence.quote: All PAA curricula are designed using modules, each with a single outcome for students to achieve.
Each Practical and Applied Arts curriculum is composed of modules configured into courses, along with suggestions for modules that are suitable for middle or secondary level survey courses.

allEvidence.observation: Each entry on the course's outcomes page is one module: the entry is titled with the module name and shows a “Module Code” (the outcome code in sk.json); the module's own page prints one “Outcome” with its indicators. The site lists the course levels under “Course Configurations”.

modules.name: Module 3: Information Processing in the Workplace (Core)
Module 99A: Extended Study (Optional)
