outcomes.statement: Improvise in a jazz style on an instrument exploring understanding of applicable jazz theory.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and analyze musical events within a solo or composition (e.g., shout chorus, form, dynamics, pitches, changes, articulation).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Play and/or transcribe recorded music of recognized performers through methods such as:
- play blues heads and simple and more complex jazz tunes by ear
- sing roots of the chord progression of the solo
- call and response with the teacher (or other students)
- sing and/or play along with solo
- sing the solo being studied without listening to the recording at the same time
- notate the solo including elements such as form, chord changes, pitches, rhythms articulations, and dynamics
- start with short sections such as a few bars or a single lick, and gradually increase the length and complexity of the selection.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Create simple, short three or four note jazz licks and develop these licks by methods such as:
- transposing
- transforming
- adding single notes
- decorating
- connecting licks with segments of scales.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Exhibit improvement and growth in the presentation and construction of improvised solos in a performance setting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Take personal and musical risks by trying new ways to express oneself in the jazz idiom, using new ideas, new concepts, and a variety of styles.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Improvise to show the beginning of understanding the function of guide tones within a musical form or chord progression.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Demonstrate, through writing, describing, and/or playing, the understanding of jazz theory including:
- 7th chords
- modes of major and minor scales
- blues form.

outcomes.statement: Explore the elements of jazz theory through personal musical performance.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare, rehearse, and perform music in a jazz style in solo, small group, or large ensemble settings.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify different elements of music such as articulation, rhythm, beat, metre, time placement, and tone that help create a jazz style and apply this knowledge while music making.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize and define musical forms emphasizing blues form, in music that is listened to and/or performed.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: As a class and with help from the teacher design, implement, and evaluate a personal plan to improve individual performance process, and to enhance knowledge and understandings of jazz (e.g., as part of the process of improvement, include recording and listening back to the performances, practices, and/or rehearsals).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe conventions regarding jazz articulation and use those conventions in performance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Know, describe, and use in performance the standard notation conventions such as note durations up to 16th notes, codas, D.S.s, and dynamic markings.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the standards of notation in jazz music that are different from traditional "classical" notation (e.g., falls, doits, turns, and hats, as well as notation conventions such as how off-beat quarter notes should be written).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Begin to use jazz vocabulary to relate jazz theory to personal musical performance (see Jazz Glossary).

outcomes.statement: Show growth in individual instrumental techniques and knowledge of the elements of music and apply these to create or show a musical product.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate and record technical development, with assistance from the teacher, and develop strategies to improve.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate technical inquiry questions and take action on the findings of the inquiry (e.g., "What can I do to get better?" or "How could I change this performance, paper, or arrangement?").

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Play with a tone appropriate to the style and personal development.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discover concepts and skills necessary to play expressively and implement through playing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Play a 1 octave chromatic scale.*

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Play major, dorian, mixolydian, and blues scales in G, C, F, Bb, Eb and Ab concert.* Sight-read music at one level below the general level of the music being performed by the ensemble.
*For students playing drum set, teachers may substitute other technique directly related to set playing, although the drummers should know the scales on mallets and perform the set techniques in addition to the mallet technique.

outcomes.statement: Listen and respond as a jazz performer when playing jazz.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Respond to qualities of personal tone such as pitch, dynamics, style, rhythm, and time.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Respond to the rest of the ensemble (e.g., their tone, pitch, dynamics, style, rhythm, time, balance, and blend).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Respond to the ensemble's response to the student's responding to them (e.g. when the lead player starts to play out or articulate a certain way, does the band follow and does the lead player recognize it?).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Respond to the conductor/leader, including his/her gestures, cues, tempo, expressions, and body language.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Listen to the acoustic properties of the performing space, including the sound, tone, loudness, and reverb of the room, and adjust playing accordingly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: React to the audience, to their presence (or not), body language, expressions, and their reaction to the music (e.g. applause, cheering, being asked to play quieter).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Know the history, culture, style, form, and tempo of the music being performed and respond to the music (written or not written) by reading the music and/or performing the notes and/or changes appropriately.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recall previous experiences and knowledge (in music and in life) and integrate these into solo and group jazz performances.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Know any special emotional context that may apply to the music, generate the appropriate emotional feeling or energy, and/or change the personal emotional state of the performer to synchronize it with the emotional context of the music being performed.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Know, predict, and/or anticipate what is next or might be next in the music and prepare for that while performing in the moment of the music.

outcomes.statement: Listen to jazz as a jazz performer when not personally playing the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to jazz music and analyze form, tone, style, era, dynamics, articulation, time signature, characteristic rhythms, time, balance, blend, key, and/or pitch.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the development of the jazz music (head, arrangement, or improvisation) as a whole or in smaller sections.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze and reflect on the structure of the chord progression and the potential development of the chord progression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the characteristic sounds, licks, tone, and other elements of well-known players and/or groups.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze jazz performances individually and in groups, to identify performers and/or groups on recordings just by listening to the characteristic sounds or ideas presented in the music.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze and reflect on just one instrument from the beginning to the end of the musical selection, (e.g., Did the player play the same way all the way through? How was it different or the same? What did he/she play that the student also might be able to play?)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze and reflect on the melody, bass line, fills (including drums and percussion), background lines, chord progression, chord roots and sing along with the recording.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the history, cultural heritage, and effect of current events as these apply to the musical selection.

outcomes.statement: Explore the ability to analyze jazz music in real time while making or listening to the music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Individually and in groups, with help from the teacher, identify, experiment with, and purposefully use strategies to solve different challenges related to music making.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common chord progressions including but not limited to blues changes in music performed and/or listened to (including progressions that break from the norm).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the time signature on first hearing a piece of music, in simple time signatures such as 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Listen to music and develop strategies to recognize aurally the time signature of the music, and when appropriate, clap on 2 and 4.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discover and apply the pattern of strong and weak beats that are identified with the above time signatures.

outcomes.statement: Individually and in groups develop and apply criteria to use in critical evaluation of performances of jazz music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to the music of the great jazz performers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate criteria of excellence through listening to the music of the great performers, (e.g., What is it that makes the music great? What do the great performers do that the student or student's ensemble do not?).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Design and implement a plan for improvement (personal and group) based on the criteria generated from listening to the great performers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: When listening to a musical selection, discover the elements of music that may be used by a listener to help identify the style, period, composer, culture, and performer. As a class, describe and classify the music using appropriate jazz language (e.g., style, period, composer, culture, and performer).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the components of listening actively, continue to develop listening skills, and recognize that listening actively contributes to the authenticity of performances.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize and discuss the value of original thought, technical proficiency, place, era, and other concepts, in the music of the great jazz performers.

outcomes.statement: Explore and begin to implement the skills, knowledge, techniques, and attitudes necessary for successful ensemble performance.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Know the basic functions of the student's individual part within an ensemble by demonstrating the ability to perform those specific tasks that are particular to the instrument that the student plays in the ensemble (e.g., comping for guitar and piano, walking lines for the bass, solo chairs in the horns).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: With direction from the teacher, identify the importance of and begin to implement attention to melodic phrasing, rhythmic accuracy, articulation, and responsibility for time, in the preparation and performance of jazz.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the challenges and importance of playing in tune with good balance and tone. Students and teachers together should develop strategies to improve the individual tuning of the students and their ensembles (e.g., who to listen to in his/her section or ensemble).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the components of a "professional" attitude towards conduct, focus, and communication skills in rehearsal, preparation of materials, and presentation of products.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Show respect for the personal work of self and others through appropriate critique.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: With direction from the teacher, critically examine and assess the student's individual work and personal contributions to group projects/performances.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Be accepting of appropriate critiques from others and work towards implementing the solutions to those critiques.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the value of individual practice and how to practice, conduct an ongoing evaluation of the student's personal practice skills, and implement a plan to improve.

outcomes.statement: Develop the ability to distinguish aurally the different eras, genres, styles, and feels of jazz by listening to and/or performing the representative music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Develop (through listening) a list or understanding of the basic characteristics of different jazz styles, genres, periods, and place and implement that knowledge into practice and performance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate aspects of jazz such as history, performers, styles, and eras through a variety of media.

outcomes.statement: Develop a jazz history timeline from about 1890 through the present, including developments in jazz music, major figures, and styles along with important world historical events.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate an awareness of key historical and artistic developments and trends as they relate to the eras and styles of jazz (e.g., Great Depression, WW II, swing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify influential performers in the history of jazz (e.g., players on the level of Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Bill Evans, Elvin Jones, Louis Armstrong) players that everyone who plays jazz should know. Investigate why these performers are identified as particularly influential and listen to their music.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the different peoples that made up the culture of New Orleans at the start of the 20th century and the ways that these cultures influenced the development of jazz music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research career avenues in jazz and music in general.

outcomes.statement: Investigate a variety of jazz styles or genres, and explore the influence of jazz on Canadian culture, past and present.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the influence of jazz in Canadian musical culture (e.g., was jazz ever the "pop" music in Canada, North America, or Europe?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe and discuss music styles other than jazz from the past and/or present that may have developed as a result of contact between different cultures.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how Canadian and international copyright laws affect the lives of those who work in the jazz field.

evidence.observation: The outcomes page groups the outcomes under 3 unit headings.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the work area.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: General Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective responsibility for, and commitment to, promoting and supporting workplace safety.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety goggles, footwear, hearing and respiratory protection, headwear and protective clothing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Review the fire evacuation plan for the work practices including the location of fire alarms, fire extinguishers and exits.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage resulting from unsafe work practices or environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in case of an injury or accident, such as whom to contact and first-aid procedures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of ventilation in a confined environment as it relates to controlling air quality (e.g., welding fumes, plastic off-gas and cutting, fluid misting).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify hazardous materials and relevant Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) procedures.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean work area and methods used to maintain a clean work area.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify risks and potential safety hazards (e.g., tools on floor, exposed live wires and extension cords).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the hierarchy of controls to control hazards and mitigate risks in machining workspaces and environments.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe control measures using the hierarchy of controls to limit risks of expected physical hazards associated with machining (e.g., workstation ergonomics, slip, trips and falls, repetitive strain).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Demonstrate an understanding of procedures (e.g., safety inspections and audits that include ergonomics of workspace lay-outs) to ensure safe practices in the machining workspace.

outcomes.statement: Apply safe work practices in the machine shop.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Machining Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify potential safety hazards (e.g., electricity, chemicals, rotating machines, ventilation and noise) in the machining work environment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate consistent and effective use of personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure personal safety and the safety of others in the workspace.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss processes involved in good housekeeping procedures and routines in the machine shop.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Locate fire extinguishers, the eye-wash station and the first-aid station in the work environment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify preventative measures to avoid specific accidents common to machining equipment and environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize potential hazards presented by tools and equipment in the machine shop.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe usage of all tools and equipment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create an emergency evacuation plan to safely leave the machine shop.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the process involved in reporting near-misses or accidents.

outcomes.statement: Explore machining as a discipline.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Introduction to Machining (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify machining as a reduction process.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the role of machining in various industries (e.g., manufacturing, forestry, mining and agriculture).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the influence of machining on everyday life (e.g., transportation and household items).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore connections between machining and other trades.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain modern changes in machining such as computer numerical control (CNC).

outcomes.statement: Explore measurement systems used in machining.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Basic Measurement (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore imperial and metric systems of measurement and their uses in machining.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between semi-precision and precision measurements.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate accurate measurements to within 1/64” (0.5 mm).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform accurate measurements of angles with a protractor.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Categorize angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Calculate angles and distances using both decimals and fractions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Interpret readings from a variety of measurement tools including dials, metres and scales.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate accurate use of advanced measurement tools.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4B: Advanced Measurement (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Perform accurate measurements using Vernier and dial calipers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Practice using various micrometers (e.g., outside, inside and depth).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate use of advanced measurement tools (e.g., telescoping gauges, gauge blocks and small hole gauges).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the accurate use of digital measurement tools to within 0.001” or 0.02 mm.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of proper care, cleaning and storage of measurement tools.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practice taking measurements with a dial indicator.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate use of dial indicators for inspection of workpieces and machine set-up.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss factors that can affect the accuracy of measurement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the history and impact of technology on the science of metrology.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in determining measurement standards.

outcomes.statement: Examine information found on a technical drawing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Using Technical Drawings (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss specific information found in the title block on a technical drawing (e.g., scale, name and tolerances).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify symbols used by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the use of standardized symbols, lines and figures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the importance of geometric tolerances and dimensions (e.g., concentricity, parallelism and orientation).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate between isometric (3D) and orthographic (2D top, front and right-side views) representations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop shop sketches of parts to be produced.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate techniques to effectively prepare materials and tools for a machining project through layout work.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Layout Work (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the value of the layout process.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the safe handling and use of layout tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of layout tools (e.g., layout dye, scriber, hermaphrodite caliper and surface gauge).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the need to protect layout equipment from being damaged.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of tools for precision layout work (e.g., Vernier height gauge, right angle plate, parallels, V-blocks and straightedge).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply layout techniques using various layout and hand tools (e.g., drill grinding gauge and right-angle square) to complete a project.

outcomes.statement: Explore the use of machining tools.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Machining Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the proper use and safety considerations for machining tools (e.g., compliance with manufacturer recommended uses and limitations).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research safety guards, how they are intended to protect the worker and the worker responsibility to report issues with the guard.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Classify machining tools (e.g., lathes, drills, grinders, mills and saws) as striking, grinding, cutting or drilling tools.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the use of measurement tools (e.g., Vernier and dial calipers).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the evolution of machining tools from the industrial revolution to present day.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore connections between project material and tool selection.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate correct storage and maintenance of machining tools according to the manufacturer.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the application of computer numerical control (CNC) and advanced machining tools.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect tools for damage and tag for repair as instructed by the supervisor.

outcomes.statement: Develop safe and efficient hand tool technique.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Hand Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify common machine shop hand tools (e.g., files, hacksaw, ball peen hammer, chisel and screwdriver).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe work practices when working with hand tools and equipment including the use of PPE recommended by the tool manufacturer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Maintain a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate risks related to the use of hand tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate the selection and use of the correct tool for a specific task.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools for damage and tag for repair as instructed by a supervisor.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective maintenance, repair and cleaning of tools.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply proper hand tool techniques to produce a project.

outcomes.statement: Explore the types of fasteners used by machinists.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices when using fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE (e.g., Unified National Coarse [UNC], Unified National Fine [UNF]), grade, length, diameter and thread pitch or count.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Decode the nomenclature associated with threaded fasteners.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the application of fasteners including pins, rivets, keys and self-locking tapers.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how adhesives and sealants are used as fasteners and how some are not compatible if mixed.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the need for safe, proper handling of adhesives.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of tightening sequence and torque values of specific fasteners.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Utilize torque wrenches to properly tighten fasteners.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Complete thread repair of damaged fasteners using a tap and die set.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to extract broken fasteners.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe the use of commercially available products to assist with the removal (e.g., penetrating oil) or securing of fasteners (e.g., Loctite).

outcomes.statement: Examine the characteristics of metals used in machining.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Metal Characteristics (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore different classifications of metals (e.g., ferrous, nonferrous, plain carbon steel, alloy steel).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss mechanical properties of metals (e.g., hardness, toughness, ductility, colouration and resistance to corrosion).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with metals.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze characteristics of specific metals using non-destructive and destructive testing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify typical uses of different types of metals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research material costs for a given project.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) material classification system (e.g., 1018, 4140 and stainless 316).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the purpose of heat treatment of metals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Heat Treatment of Metals (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the reasons for heat-treating metals.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the properties and characteristics of metals that can be heat-treated.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Demonstrate heat treatment on a sample or project material.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when heat-treating metals.

outcomes.statement: Examine surface finishing techniques and their applications.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Metal Finishing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how the finish of a machined surface is designated using a set of numbers and symbols indicating roughness.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between the quality of a machined surface and production costs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of surface finish with respect to application.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify potential hazards associated with finishing processes and tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate finishing techniques (e.g., polishing, lapping, grinding and filing).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine speeds and feeds of typical machining tools as they relate to required surface finish.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare completed project with samples of surface finishes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when finishing metal.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply appropriate finishing techniques to achieve specific surface finishes.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore inorganic coatings used in finishing metals.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe and effective use of jigs and fixtures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Jigs and Fixtures (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify specific applications for jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how to use jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Design a simple jig to guide a drill bit to create a hole or assist with a project.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design a simple fixture to be used with a lathe, grinder or drill press.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore industrial efficiencies created by using jigs and fixtures.

outcomes.statement: Explore safe and effective use of cutting fluids.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Cutting Fluids (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe working practices, storage and disposal of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the purpose of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Review the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for each cutting fluid.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the properties and function of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare samples of various cutting fluids.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the properties of cutting oils and water-soluble coolants.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research industrial applications of cutting fluids.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the safe and effective operation of drilling machines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Drills and Drilling Machines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the styles and types of drilling machines.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Review safety rules, including the effective use of personal protective equipment (PPE), that must be followed while using drilling machines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the parts of a drill press.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practice using appropriate devices (e.g., jigs and fixtures) to hold material.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the various operations (e.g., drilling, countersinking, counterboring, reaming and spot-facing) that can be performed using a drill press.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Calculate and adjust spindle speed revolutions per minute (rpm) and feed rate.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with drilling machines.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Conduct maintenance of equipment, including inspecting and sharpening drill bits.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore industrial applications of drilling machines.

outcomes.statement: Investigate safe and effective use of saws and cutoff machines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Saws and Cutoff Machines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List various types of saws and cutoff machines (e.g., horizontal band, vertical band and abrasive cutoff).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore safety procedures for safe and effective use of saws and cutoff machines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with saws and cutoff machines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the safe preparation of cutting materials.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe machine maintenance including inspection and replacement of blades.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Select the appropriate blade for cutting different metals considering thickness and hardness of material.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and correct sawing problems (e.g., drifting cut, improper blade tension, worn blades, improper positioning and securing of material).

outcomes.statement: Explore safe and effective use of grinders and abrasives.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 33: Grinding and Abrasives (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify grinding wheels and abrasives used in the machining shop.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss potential safety hazards associated with grinding.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to properly adjust guards and safety devices on grinding equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the use of grinding agents and abrasives.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore connections between modern grinding processes and traditional First Nation and Métis grinding/reduction techniques.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare applications of dry- and wet-type grinders.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List the characteristics of different types of abrasives used for grinding wheels considering size, shape, thickness, abrasive size and type, bonding agent, hardness and operating speed limitations.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify surface finishes required for various applications.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore polishing materials and techniques required to achieve specific finishes.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with grinders and abrasives.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Sharpen a variety of tool cutting edges.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective grinding techniques to reduce material to specifications.

outcomes.statement: Explore career opportunities in the machining trades.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 44: Career Opportunities in Machining (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the relationship between machining and different types of manufacturing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a list of personal interests, skills and traits that could lead to a career in the agricultural equipment trade.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate related occupations in the machining trade (e.g., automotive machinist, tool and die makers, metallurgist and millwrights).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research which machining-related occupations are facing shortages, and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally or provincially.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities common to people involved in machining-related occupations.

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Research technical training options (e.g., Saskatchewan Polytechnic, Northern Alberta Institute of Technology and Southern Alberta Institute of Technology) for the machining trades.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Participate in a field trip to a local machine shop.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Conduct an interview of a journeyperson to gain an understanding of local careers in the machining trades.

indicators.label: j

evidence.quote: All Practical and Applied Arts curricula are designed using modules, each with a single outcome for students to achieve.

allEvidence.quote: All Practical and Applied Arts curricula are designed using modules, each with a single outcome for students to achieve.
Each Practical and Applied Arts curriculum is composed of modules configured into courses, along with suggestions for modules that are suitable for middle or secondary level survey courses.

allEvidence.observation: Each entry on the course's outcomes page is one module: the entry is titled with the module name and shows a “Module Code” (the outcome code in sk.json); the module's own page prints one “Outcome” with its indicators. The site lists the course levels under “Course Configurations”.

modules.name: Module 99A: Extended Study (Optional)
modules.note: Extended Study: the site prints no outcome statement for it, so the dataset leaves it out.

courses.name: Mechanical and Automotive 10, A20, B20, A30, B30

outcomes.statement: Develop an awareness of the automotive industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Automotive Industry (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the history of the automobile and automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and explain the operation of an automobile’s major systems (e.g., steering, suspension, brakes, drive train, cooling, lubrication, engine).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe processes used to identify automotive system faults.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the automotive workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Automotive Safety Equipment, Hazardous Materials, and Housekeeping Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the importance of safety when undertaking automotive service procedures, including safety hazards and preventative measures common to the automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect and utilize protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE), such as safety goggles, hearing protection, gloves and footwear, and appropriate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential health concerns when PPE is not used properly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the correct fire extinguisher for different classifications (i.e., A, B, C, D and K) of fires and how to use the extinguisher correctly (i.e., PASS - Pull Aim Squeeze Sweep).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean workplace and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Locate, identify and explain the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station and first aid station) in the workplace.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

outcomes.statement: Explore factors to consider related to vehicle purchase.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare a budget prior to purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between personal wants and needs based on a specific budget.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss factors (e.g., environmental impact of a vehicle, the cost of operations and potential repair costs) to consider when purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify vehicles that fit criteria based on personal budget, wants and needs.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze potential vehicles for purchase based on customer, commercial and technical reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain and/or perform procedures for inspecting and testing vehicles before purchase.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify safety practices to follow when inspecting and testing vehicles.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Estimate potential repair costs of any service or repair needed for a used vehicle.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain insurance, financing and warranty options for purchasing or leasing a new or used vehicle.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain hand and power tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Hand and Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with hand and power tools, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify tools according to their capabilities (e.g., cutting, striking and holding) and method of power (e.g., hand, power, electric and hydraulic).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Maintain and store tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize that metric and imperial systems of measurement are both used in the automotive industry.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify, select and use appropriate tools for specific tasks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools before use and tag for repair as required.

outcomes.statement: Identify, select and use automotive fasteners properly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Automotive Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with automotive fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common categories (e.g., clips, pins, nuts, bolts, washers, screws and rivets) of automotive fasteners.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE, grade, length, diameter and thread pitch.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe types (e.g., hex, 12 point and Torx) of fastener heads commonly found in automotive applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of torqueing fasteners, including following a fastener tightening sequence.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine torque values and sequences for specific fasteners.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Adjust and use torque wrenches and/or angle gauges to properly tighten fasteners.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform fastener related tasks such as extraction, thread repair and tap and die selection and use.

outcomes.statement: Explain the characteristics of automotive lubricants.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Automotive Lubricants (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the functions and properties of automotive fluids and lubricants.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between synthetic and non-synthetic lubricants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between different oil service ratings (e.g., SAE viscosity grades, API service ratings and original equipment manufacturer [OEM] specifications).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function of various oil additives.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain ways in which oil can be contaminated and the potential effects of contaminated oil on an engine.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain safe and sustainable procedures for disposal of automotive fluids, containers and components.

outcomes.statement: Maintain outdoor power and recreation equipment following appropriate procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9B: Outdoor Power and Recreation Equipment Maintenance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with outdoor power and recreation equipment, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify components of outdoor power and recreation equipment that require periodic lubrication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Perform general maintenance (e.g., check belt tension, inspect spark plug and perform winterization procedures) on outdoor power and recreation equipment and accessories such as blades, augers and tines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate the condition of drive mechanisms (e.g., chains, belts, pulleys and continuously variable transmissions [CVTs]) on outdoor power and recreation equipment.

outcomes.statement: Explain basic automotive maintenance procedures.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify appropriate safety procedures related to automotive maintenance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain common procedures for periodic inspection and testing of automobiles.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain common procedures to perform automotive maintenance based on manufacturers' specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify and inspect basic components (e.g., tires, fluid levels, wipers, lights) of an automobile that require periodic inspection and/or lubrication.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive tires and wheels.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Automotive Tires and Wheels (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., follow proper inflation procedures to avoid explosive hazards and be aware of cut and pinch points) when working with automotive tires and wheels, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how tire condition affects vehicle handling, fuel economy and safety characteristics.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the design and construction of tires and wheels, including tire sidewall information.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Choose the correct tire size and type according to manufacturer’s recommendations for specific vehicle and performance applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the consequences of installing tires of inappropriate sizes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate tire condition (e.g., tread depth, wear patterns and rubber condition) and explain causes and effects of tire damage, wear and defects.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain when and why tire service, such as tire rotation and balancing, is required.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Perform tire and wheel related service operations such as rotation, dismounting and mounting, balancing and repair.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) repair, relearn and programming procedures.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all tires and wheels and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the operation and repair of small engines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Small Engines (Core) · Suggested Time: 30-40 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of pinch points, hot surfaces, sharp surfaces and moving parts) when working with small engines, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the operating principles of an internal combustion engine.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between 2-stroke and 4-stroke engine operation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the construction and function of major engine sub-assemblies, including the cylinder block, head, and valve train.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate how repair manuals can guide engine disassembly, repair, and reassembly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the relationship and operation of major engine components.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Define and determine engine measurements, such as clearance, out of round and taper.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how improper lubrication or cooling can contribute to engine failure.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify types of specialized measuring equipment and use appropriate procedures to measure and evaluate engine condition.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Disassemble and reassemble an operational small engine.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Use appropriate procedures to start, run and stop a small engine.

outcomes.statement: Explore mechanical and automotiverelated occupations.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a list of personal interests, skills and traits that could lead to a career in the mechanical and automotive trade.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate occupations in the mechanical and automotive trade (e.g., automotive service technician, parts management technician, automotive parts person, service writer, service manager, automotive designer and automotive engineer).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research which mechanical and automotive-related occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally or provincially.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities common to people involved in mechanical and automotive-related jobs.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Explore opportunities for underrepresented populations in the automotive industry.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research experience and qualifications for newcomers to enter the mechanical and automotive industry.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Communicate research findings related to mechanical and automotiverelated occupations through a display, brochure, video, presentation software, website or an oral presentation.

indicators.text: generates and uses criteria to self-assess and set goals for improvement as a speaker, presenter, viewer and listener;

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: appraises own and others' work for clarity;

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: identifies and analyzes effectiveness of a variety of language strategies;

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: states appropriate and achievable improvement goals based on self-analysis; chooses and applies strategies appropriate to improvement goals and reflect on progress in achieving those goals; and,

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: sets goals to improve viewing, listening, speaking and representing.

items.text: Explore historical and contemporary elements of the social environment and personal identity.

Explore using Michif French for following protocol when welcoming visitors and Elders/Lii pleu vyeu (e.g., welcoming into a space, offering a gift or tobacco, pulling out a chair, offering tea, serving of food).

Explore using Michif French while completing routine tasks of the home and classroom (e.g., washing dishes, tidying the house/class, laundry, wiping the table, help to prepare a meal, setting the table).
Explore how routine tasks in the home and classroom have changed over time.
Investigate local historical and contemporary spaces, businesses or schools by reaching out to community members for information, stories, and support.
Investigate opportunities in Saskatchewan to participate in Michif French culture with the guidance of a Language Carrier or Lii pleu vyeu.
Begin to develop relationships by visiting with local community members, Language Carriers, Elders, collectives, clubs and local Métis organizations.

Apply, with support, a variety of before, during, and after comprehension strategies to construct meaning in Michif French written texts and oral communications, with the guidance of a Language Carrier or Lii pleu vyeu.
Learn through la manyair dis promnii (e.g., with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, family, peers or learning circles) both inside and outside of the classroom.

Review interpretation of written texts and oral communications, after reading and listening, using strategies such as:
• discussing key words in oral and written texts;
• making connections between new information, prior knowledge and personal experience; and,
• reacting with emotion (e.g., empathy, surprise, appreciation or dislike).

Begin to develop personal language learning tools (e.g., classroom/personal Michif French Dictionary, self-created pronunciation audio files) on topics such as home items, routines, hobbies and foods.

Consult resources (e.g., Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, family, Michif French dictionaries and mobile apps, anchor charts, websites) and visual aids (e.g., pictures, graphs and drawings) to help construct meaning of written texts and oral communications.
Apply, with support, a variety of strategies to produce Michif French written texts and oral communications.
Learn through la manyair dis promnii (e.g., with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, family, peers).
Explore how interactions with the land contribute to authentic Michif French language acquisition.
Explore the Michif French language for personal communication on topics, such as introductions, greetings, general interactions, phrases to participate in a discussion.
Use tools such as graphic organizers and outlines to make a plan for speaking or writing.

Consult resources (e.g., Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, family, Michif French dictionaries and mobile apps, anchor charts and websites) and visual aids (e.g., pictures, graphs and drawings) to support the production of oral and written texts.

Discuss how to take risks, try unfamiliar approaches, and experiment with various forms of expression (e.g., reduce anxiety by using mental techniques, such as positive self-talk and humour, to instill confidence).
Identify prior knowledge for personal expression in Michif French.
Describe physical (e.g., gestures and facial expressions) and auditory (e.g., laughter, tone, volume) cues to convey meaning.
Retell (in English) a Michif French oral communication with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, or family members.
Demonstrate a short dialogue (e.g., practise, rehearse, role-play) with classmates in Michif French.
Reflect on personal strengths and needs with respect to one’s Michif French language and culture learning journey.
Determine personals strengths as a language learner.
Identify personal needs related to speaking, listening, reading, and writing in Michif French.
Recognize that risk-taking and a positive attitude are part of effective language learning.
Identify how la manyair dis promnii helps to meet personal language learning needs.
Celebrate personal Michif French language learning successes.

Reflect on identity through the Michif/Métis worldview and language by considering questions such as:
• How does la manyair dis promnii help to improve my understanding of the Michif French language and worldview?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand my social environments?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand my own identity?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand the Michif culture and community?
Identify, with support, when listening and reading, Michif French language concepts including basic context- specific vocabulary, word order and linguistic conventions.

Recognize context-specific and common vocabulary (e.g., lii zhours – days, lii mwaan – months, lii zoochii a likol – school supplies, paarchu dju korr – parts of the body, lii maanzhii - food, lii noombr - numbers).
Discuss the use of singular personal pronouns (e.g., Ji, Ja, Je, Tchu, Ta, y, il, ell).
Identify appropriate prepositions in context (e.g., annaryayr - behind, annavaan – in front of, dissu – on top of, ennhou - above, akoootii – beside, didaan – inside).
Recognize directional terms in context (e.g., dret - right, goosh - left, nor – north, sud – south, ouest - west, lest – east).
Recognize definite (e.g., le la, lay, lii) and indefinite articles (e.g., aen, de, day, dii).
Explain simple sentences in context (e.g., Netway la taab - Clean the table, Monnom ay – My name is, Je rest a – I live in, Jem sa maanzhii – I like to eat).
Identify, when speaking and writing, Michif French language concepts including basic context-specific vocabulary, word order and linguistic conventions.

Recognize context-specific and common vocabulary (e.g., lii zhours – days, lii mwaan – months, lii zoochii a likol – school supplies, paarchu dju korr – parts of the body, lii maanzhii - food, lii noombr - numbers).
Recognize the use of singular personal pronouns (e.g., Ji, Ja, Je, Tchu, Ta, y, il, ell).
Utilize appropriate body language and tone when speaking.
Respond to prepositions in context (e.g., annaryayr - behind, annavaan – in front of, dissu – on top of, ennhou - above, akoootii – beside, didaan – inside).
Recognize directional terms in context (e.g., dret - right, goosh - left, nor – north, sud – south, ouest - west, lest – east).
Recognize definite (e.g., le la, lay, lii) and indefinite articles (e.g., aen, de, day, dii).
Repeat simple sentences in context (e.g., Netway la taab - Clean the table, Monnom ay – My name is, Je rest a – I live in, Jem sa maanzhii – I like to eat).
Construct meaning, with support, of a variety of simple oral non-fiction and fiction Michif French communications on familiar topics.

Listen to or view a variety of simple oral Michif French communications (e.g., how to videos, storytelling videos, in-person visiting, songs) that address big ideas:
• elements of social environment;
• elements of personal identity; and,
• elements of Michif French culture.
Interpret simple oral communications or conversations.
Respond appropriately in structured interactions with common, simple, short phrases.
Respond to simple questions regarding personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, interests, and hobbies).
Compare information related to others’ personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, interests, and hobbies).
Describe personal reactions to simple oral communications with emotion (e.g., empathy, surprise, appreciation or dislike).
Construct meaning, with support, of a variety of simple written non-fiction and fiction Michif French texts on familiar topics.

Read a variety of simple written Michif French texts (e.g., children’s books, recipes, dictionaries, conversational sentences) that address elements of:
• the social environment;
• personal identity; and,
• Michif French culture.
Comprehend simple labels within the school in Michif French.
Repeat the basic directions of written imperative texts.
Respond to a survey regarding personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, Treaty area, hobbies, age, preferred foods).
Identify the vocabulary words in context in written texts on familiar topics.
Discuss the possible variations within the written orthography of Michif French based on regional variation or language carrier preference.
Describe personal reaction to written texts with emotion (e.g., empathy, surprise, appreciation or dislike).
Produce, with support, a variety of simple oral non-fiction and fiction Michif French communications on familiar topics.

Produce simple oral Michif French communications related to elements of:
• the social environment;
• personal identity; and,
• Michif French culture.
Pose questions to generate conversations on familiar topics such as hobbies, family members and class schedules.
Respond appropriately to other speakers during conversations or discussion.
Express feelings and emotions using simple adjectives, facial expressions and body language.
Convey opinions or personal perspectives on a given topic such as a fashion, music, or food.
Provide basic step-by-step instructions in situations such as cooking and giving directions to a location.
Communicate information about time.
Produce personal greetings (e.g., on the phone, in video recordings, in person).
Explain personal lived experiences or activities.
Use Michif French language for entertainment and personal enjoyment (e.g., express humour, perform skits or songs and create stories).
Produce, with support, a variety of simple written non-fiction and fiction Michif French texts on familiar topics.

Produce simple written Michif French texts related to elements of:
• the social environment;
• personal identity; and,
• Michif French culture.
Write about a variety of daily topics, such as personal details (e.g., name and age), dates (e.g., days of the week, months, seasons) and school/classroom items and routine.
Communicate simple written expressions (e.g., wii - yes, noo - no, sil voo play - please, maarsii –thank you, bonn mataen - good morning, boon apray mijii - good afternoon, Je regret - I’m sorry).
Compose a greeting card (e.g., Bonn Fayt- birthday, maarsii – thank you, Schwettchu vyen bayn - I hope you get well soon) using simple expressions.
Create simple social media posts using basic vocabulary (e.g., personal introduction, homeland).
Provide basic written directions to a place within the school or community using imperative sentences.
Experiment with communicating messages in a variety of written formats (e.g., notes, lists, paragraphs, graphs, emails, blogs and text messages).
Draft descriptions of personal lived experiences or activities related to the big ideas.
Explore the use of Michif French phonetic orthography based on regional variations or language carrier preference.

notes: Structure as printed: one section per level ('Michif French 10/20/30 Outcomes and Indicators'), each grouped under the four goal headings Culture (CU), Strategies (ST), Language Knowledge (LK) and Applications (AP). Units here are those goal headings within a level. Outcome codes: goal + course level + number (legend p. 17 printed). Indicators are lettered a., b., …; bullet sub-lists inside an indicator are kept on their own lines ('• …').
The text mixes English with Michif French words (e.g. 'Lii pleu vyeu', 'la manyair dis prominii'); they are copied as printed, including their spelling and diacritics.

All feedback must be received by June 1, 2027.'
